sentences.zh: 起閼逢閹茂，盡玄黓執徐，凡十九年。

translations.literal: From Emao in the cycle Qimao through Xuanxi Zhisu; nineteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Emao in the cycle Qimao through Xuanxi Zhisu—nineteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 1荊軻至咸陽，因王寵臣蒙嘉卑辭以求見，王大喜，朝服，設九賓而見之。

translations.literal: 1. Jing Ke reached Xianyang; through the king's favorite minister Meng Jia he used humble words to seek an audience. The king was greatly pleased, put on court dress, and received him with the ninefold guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Jing Ke arrived at Xianyang. Through the king's favorite Meng Jia he pleaded humbly for an audience. The king was delighted, donned court robes, and received him with the full nine-guest ceremony.

sentences.zh: 荊軻奉圖以進於王，圖窮而匕首見，因把王袖而揕之；

translations.literal: Jing Ke presented the map to advance it to the king; when the map was unrolled the dagger appeared, and he seized the king's sleeve and stabbed at him;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke offered up the map. When it was unrolled to the end the dagger appeared; he seized the king's sleeve and struck at him;

sentences.zh: 未至身，王驚起，袖絕。

translations.literal: before it reached his body the king started up in alarm and the sleeve tore away.
translations.idiomatic: before the blade reached him the king leapt up in terror—and the sleeve tore free.

sentences.zh: 荊軻逐王，王環柱而走。

translations.literal: Jing Ke pursued the king; the king ran around a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke chased him; the king fled around a pillar.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆愕，卒起不意，盡失其度。

translations.literal: The ministers were all stunned; the sudden event was beyond expectation, and all lost their composure.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers stood frozen. The attack came without warning; every man lost his bearing.

sentences.zh: 而秦法，群臣侍殿上者不得操尺寸之兵，左右以手共搏之，且曰：「王負劍！

translations.literal: Yet by Qin law, ministers attending in the hall might not carry weapons even a foot long; those at the king's sides grappled with their bare hands and cried: "Sire, draw your sword on your back!
translations.idiomatic: By Qin law, no courtier in the hall might carry even a hand's-length of steel; those beside the throne grappled with bare hands and shouted: "Sire—draw the sword on your back!

sentences.zh: 」負劍，王遂拔以擊荊軻，斷其左股。

translations.literal: " Drawing the sword on his back, the king then pulled it out and struck Jing Ke, severing his left thigh.
translations.idiomatic: " The king slung the sword behind him, drew it, and struck Jing Ke, cutting through his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 荊軻廢，乃引匕首擿王，中銅柱。

translations.literal: Jing Ke, crippled, then flung the dagger at the king; it struck a bronze pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Crippled, Jing Ke hurled his dagger at the king; it struck a bronze pillar.

sentences.zh: 自知事不就，罵曰：「事所以不成者，以欲生劫之，必得約契以報太子也！

translations.literal: Knowing the affair would not succeed, he cursed: "The reason it failed is that I meant to seize him alive and had to obtain a treaty to report to the crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing all was lost, he cursed: "It failed because I meant to take him alive—I had to secure a treaty to bring back to the crown prince!

sentences.zh: 」遂體解荊軻以徇。

translations.literal: " He was then dismembered and Jing Ke's body was displayed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " They dismembered Jing Ke and put his body on public display.

sentences.zh: 王於是大怒，益發兵詣趙，就王翦以伐燕，與燕師、代師戰於易水之西，大破之。

translations.literal: The king was then greatly enraged, sent more troops to Zhao, joined Wang Jian to attack Yan, and fought the Yan and Dai armies west of the Yi River, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The king in fury raised more troops, marched to Zhao, joined Wang Jian against Yan, and west of the Yi River shattered the Yan and Dai armies together.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，王翦拔薊，燕王及太子率其精兵東保遼東，李信急追之。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, Wang Jian took Ji; the king of Yan and the crown prince led their elite troops east to hold Liaodong, and Li Xin pressed hard in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In the tenth month of winter Wang Jian took Ji. The king of Yan and the crown prince fled east with their best troops to hold Liaodong; Li Xin pressed close behind.

sentences.zh: 代王嘉遺燕王書，令殺太子丹以獻。

translations.literal: King Jia of Dai sent a letter to the king of Yan ordering him to kill Crown Prince Dan and offer him up.
translations.idiomatic: King Jia of Dai wrote the king of Yan urging him to kill Crown Prince Dan and send his head as tribute.

sentences.zh: 丹匿衍水中，燕王使使斬丹，欲以獻王，王復進兵攻之。

translations.literal: Dan hid on the Yan River; the king of Yan sent an envoy to behead Dan, intending to present him to the king of Qin, but the king of Qin advanced again to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Dan hid on the Yan River. The king of Yan sent men to cut off his head, meaning to present it to Qin—but the king of Qin marched again to attack.

sentences.zh: 2王賁伐楚，取十餘城。

translations.literal: 2. Wang Ben attacked Chu and took more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Wang Ben attacked Chu and seized more than ten cities.

sentences.zh: 王問於將軍李信曰：「吾欲取荊，於將軍度用幾何人而足？

translations.literal: The king asked General Li Xin: "I wish to take Jing. In your estimate, how many men would suffice?
translations.idiomatic: The king asked General Li Xin: "I mean to take Chu. How many men do you reckon I need?

sentences.zh: 」李信曰：「不過用二十萬。

translations.literal: " Li Xin said: "No more than two hundred thousand will be needed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xin said: "No more than two hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 」王以問王翦，王翦曰：「非六十萬人不可。

translations.literal: " The king asked Wang Jian; Wang Jian said: "Without six hundred thousand men it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " The king asked Wang Jian. Wang Jian said: "It cannot be done with fewer than six hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「王將軍老矣，何怯也！

translations.literal: " The king said: "General Wang, you are old—how timid!
translations.idiomatic: " The king said: "General Wang, you have grown old. How timid you have become!"

translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian pleaded illness and withdrew to Pinyang.

translations.literal: 1. Wang Ben attacked Wei, diverting the river channels to flood Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Wang Ben attacked Wei and diverted the rivers to flood Daliang.

sentences.zh: 魏王假降，殺之，遂滅魏。

translations.literal: King Jia of Wei surrendered; they killed him and extinguished Wei.
translations.idiomatic: King Jia of Wei surrendered. They killed him and extinguished Wei.

sentences.zh: 王使人謂安陵君曰：「寡人欲以五百里地易安陵。

translations.literal: The king sent someone to tell Lord Anling: "I wish to exchange five hundred li of territory for Anling.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent word to Lord Anling: "I wish to trade five hundred li of land for your state of Anling."

sentences.zh: 」安陵君曰：「大王加惠，以大易小，甚幸。

translations.literal: " Lord Anling said: "Your Majesty shows favor in offering the large for the small—greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: " Lord Anling said: "Your Majesty honors me by offering the greater for the lesser. I am most fortunate."

sentences.zh: 雖然，臣受地於魏之先王，願終守之，弗敢易。

translations.literal: Even so, I received this land from Wei's former kings; I wish to guard it to the end and dare not exchange it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I received this land from the former kings of Wei. I mean to hold it to the end and dare not trade it away."

sentences.zh: 」王義而許之。

translations.literal: " The king approved his righteousness and consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The king honored his integrity and let the matter stand.

sentences.zh: 會城父，楚人因隨之，三日三夜不頓舍，大敗李信，入兩壁，殺七都尉；

translations.literal: at Chengfü. The men of Chu followed close upon them; for three days and three nights they did not halt camp, routed Li Xin utterly, entered both camps, and killed seven commandants;
translations.idiomatic: at Chengfü. Chu pressed hard on their heels; for three days and three nights they never made camp, shattered Li Xin, overran both camps, and killed seven commandants;

sentences.zh: 李信奔還。

translations.literal: Li Xin fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin fled home in defeat.

sentences.zh: 王聞之，大怒，自〔馳〕至頻陽，〔見〕謝王翦曰<ref>自〔馳〕至頻陽〔見〕謝王翦曰據《史記·王翦列傳》補。

translations.literal: When the king heard, he was greatly enraged; he himself [galloped] to Pinyang, [saw] and apologized to Wang Jian, saying<ref>He himself [galloped] to Pinyang, [saw] and apologized to Wang Jian, saying—supplemented per the "Biography of Wang Jian" in the Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: When the king heard, he flew into a rage, [galloped] himself to Pinyang, [saw] Wang Jian and apologized, saying<ref>He [galloped] himself to Pinyang, [saw] Wang Jian and apologized, saying—supplemented per the Shiji "Biography of Wang Jian."

sentences.zh: </ref>：「寡人不用將軍謀，李信果辱秦軍。

translations.literal: </ref>: "I did not follow the general's counsel; Li Xin has indeed shamed the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>: "I ignored your counsel, and Li Xin has indeed shamed the Qin army."

sentences.zh: 〔今聞荊兵日進而西〕<ref>〔今聞荊兵日進而西〕據《史記·王翦列傳》補。

translations.literal: [Now I hear the Chu army advances westward day by day]<ref>[Now I hear the Chu army advances westward day by day]—supplemented per the "Biography of Wang Jian" in the Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: [Now I hear Chu presses westward day by day]<ref>[Now I hear Chu presses westward day by day]—supplemented per the Shiji "Biography of Wang Jian."

sentences.zh: </ref>，將軍雖病，獨忍棄寡人乎！

translations.literal: </ref> General, though you are ill, can you bear to abandon me!
translations.idiomatic: </ref> General, though you are ill—can you bear to leave me in the lurch?"

sentences.zh: 」王翦謝病不能將，王曰：「已矣，勿復言！

translations.literal: " Wang Jian declined on grounds of illness that he could not command; the king said: "Enough—speak no more of it!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian pleaded illness and said he could not command. The king said: "Enough. Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 」王翦曰：「〔大王〕必不得已用臣<ref>〔大王〕必不得已用臣據《史記·王翦列傳》補。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "[Your Majesty], if you must use me<ref>[Your Majesty], if you must use me—supplemented per the "Biography of Wang Jian" in the Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "[Your Majesty], if you must have me<ref>[Your Majesty], if you must have me—supplemented per the Shiji "Biography of Wang Jian."

sentences.zh: </ref>，非六十萬人不可！

translations.literal: </ref>, without six hundred thousand men it cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, it cannot be done without six hundred thousand men!"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「為聽將軍計耳。

translations.literal: " The king said: "Very well—I will follow the general's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The king said: "Done. I will follow your plan."

sentences.zh: 」於是王翦將六十萬人伐楚。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Wang Jian led six hundred thousand men against Chu.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian then took six hundred thousand men against Chu.

sentences.zh: 王送至霸上，王翦請美田宅甚眾。

translations.literal: The king saw him off to Bashang; Wang Jian asked for many fine fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: The king saw him off as far as Bashang. Wang Jian asked for a great many fine estates.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「將軍行矣，何憂貧乎！

translations.literal: The king said: "General, you are on your way—why worry about poverty!
translations.idiomatic: The king said: "General, you are marching—why fear poverty?"

sentences.zh: 」王翦曰：「為大王將，有功，終不得封侯，故及大王之向臣，以請田宅為子孫業耳。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Serving Your Majesty as a general, though I have merit I shall never be enfeoffed as marquis; therefore while Your Majesty still faces me I ask for fields and houses as my descendants' estate.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "As your general I may win merit yet never be made a marquis. While you still heed me, I ask only fields and houses as my children's inheritance."

sentences.zh: 」王大笑。

translations.literal: " The king laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " The king laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 王翦既行，至關，使使還請善田者五輩。

translations.literal: After Wang Jian had marched, when he reached the pass he sent envoys back five times to request more fine fields.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Jian had marched, at the frontier pass he sent messengers back five times to ask for yet more fine land.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「將軍之乞貸亦已甚矣！

translations.literal: Someone said: "The general's begging and borrowing has gone too far!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "The general's begging has gone too far!"

sentences.zh: 」王翦曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "Not so."

sentences.zh: 王怚中而不信人，今空國中之甲士而專委於我，我不多請田宅為子孫業以自堅，顧令王坐而疑我矣。

translations.literal: The king is harsh in temperament and does not trust men. Now he has emptied the state's armored soldiers and entrusted them wholly to me; if I do not ask abundantly for fields and houses as my descendants' estate to make myself secure, I would instead let the king sit and suspect me.
translations.idiomatic: The king is suspicious by nature and trusts no one. He has emptied the realm of its soldiers and placed them all in my hands. Unless I ask loudly for land and houses as my children's patrimony—to make myself look harmless—he will sit on his throne and doubt me."

sentences.zh: 1王翦取陳以南至平輿。

translations.literal: 1. Wang Jian took the region from Chen south to Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Wang Jian took everything from Chen south to Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 楚人聞王翦益軍而來，乃悉國中兵以御之；

translations.literal: When the men of Chu heard Wang Jian was coming with reinforced troops, they mustered all the armies in the state to oppose him;
translations.idiomatic: When Chu heard Wang Jian was coming with a greater host, they mustered every soldier in the realm to meet him;

sentences.zh: 王翦堅壁不與戰。

translations.literal: Wang Jian fortified his camps and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian walled his camps and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 楚人數挑戰，終不出。

translations.literal: The men of Chu challenged again and again; he never came out.
translations.idiomatic: Chu challenged again and again; he never stirred.

sentences.zh: 王翦日休士洗沐，而善飲食，撫循之；

translations.literal: Day by day Wang Jian rested the soldiers, let them bathe, gave them good food and drink, and comforted them;
translations.idiomatic: Day after day Wang Jian rested his men, let them wash, fed them well, and soothed them;

sentences.zh: 親與士卒同食。

translations.literal: he ate with the soldiers in person.
translations.idiomatic: he ate with the rank and file himself.

sentences.zh: 久之，王翦使人問：「軍中戲乎？

translations.literal: After a long while Wang Jian sent someone to ask: "Are they at play in camp?
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Wang Jian sent to ask: "What games are the men playing?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「方投石、超距。

translations.literal: " The reply came: "They are just now hurling stones and leaping in the long-jump drill.
translations.idiomatic: " The answer came: "Stone-casting and long jumps."

sentences.zh: 」王翦曰：「可用矣！

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "They are fit to be used!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "They are ready!"

sentences.zh: 」楚既不得戰，乃引而東。

translations.literal: " Since Chu could not bring him to battle, they withdrew east.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu, unable to draw him out, marched east.

sentences.zh: 王翦追之，令壯士擊，大破楚師，至蘄南，殺其將軍項燕，楚師遂敗走。

translations.literal: Wang Jian pursued, ordered the picked men to strike, routed the Chu army utterly, reached south of Qi, killed their general Xiang Yan, and the Chu army fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian pursued, ordered his best men forward, shattered the Chu host, reached south of Qi, killed their general Xiang Yan, and Chu broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 王翦因乘勝略定城邑。

translations.literal: Wang Jian then rode the victory to seize and settle the cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian then pressed the victory and pacified city after city.

sentences.zh: 1大興兵，使王賁攻遼東，虜燕王喜。

translations.literal: 1. Qin raised a great army and sent Wang Ben to attack Liaodong, capturing King Xi of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Qin mobilized on a great scale and sent Wang Ben against Liaodong, capturing King Xi of Yan.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：燕丹不勝一朝之忿以犯虎狼之秦，輕慮淺謀，挑怨速禍，使召公之廟不祀忽諸，罪孰大焉！

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: Crown Prince Dan, unable to master a morning's wrath, provoked tiger-and-wolf Qin with shallow counsel and light scheming, inviting enmity and hastening disaster, so that Duke Shao's temple sacrifices ceased in a trice—what crime could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: Crown Prince Dan could not master a single morning's rage and struck at Qin, tiger and wolf among states—shallow in counsel, reckless in plan, inviting hatred and hurrying ruin, until Duke Shao's temple stood empty overnight. What crime could be greater?

sentences.zh: 而論者或謂之賢，豈不過哉！

translations.literal: Yet some commentators call him worthy—have they not gone too far!
translations.idiomatic: Yet some writers call him noble. Have they not praised him far too much?

sentences.zh: ::夫為國家者，任官以才，立政以禮，懷民以仁，交鄰以信。

translations.literal: :: For one who governs a state: appoint officials by talent, establish policy by ritual, cherish the people with benevolence, treat neighbors with good faith.
translations.idiomatic: :: Who rules a state appoints men by talent, governs by ritual, holds the people with benevolence, and deals with neighbors in good faith.

sentences.zh: 是以官得其人，政得其節，百姓懷其德，四鄰親其義。

translations.literal: Thus offices gain the right men, policy gains the right measure, the hundred clans embrace its virtue, and the four neighbors are drawn to its righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Then offices hold the right men, policy keeps its proper measure, the people embrace its virtue, and the four quarters honor its righteousness.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則國家安如磐石，熾如焱火。

translations.literal: When this is so, the state is secure as bedrock, blazing as flame.
translations.idiomatic: Then the state stands firm as bedrock and burns hot as flame.

sentences.zh: 觸之者碎，犯之者焦，雖有強暴之國，尚何足畏哉！

translations.literal: Who touches it is shattered; who offends it is scorched—even if there is a violent state, what is there left to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Touch it and you shatter; strike it and you burn. What violent kingdom could still be feared?

sentences.zh: 丹釋此不為，顧以萬乘之國，決匹夫之怒，逞盜賊之謀，功隳身戮，社稷為墟，不亦悲哉！

translations.literal: Dan abandoned this and did not do it; instead, with a state of ten thousand chariots, he settled a common man's wrath and indulged a robber's plot—merit destroyed, body slain, altars in ruins—is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Dan cast this aside. With a realm of ten thousand chariots he indulged a private man's rage and a thief's design—merit undone, body slain, the altars ashes. Is it not pitiful?

translations.literal: :: As for kneeling and crawling prostrate—that is not true respect;
translations.idiomatic: :: Kneeling and crawling prostrate is not true respect;

sentences.zh: 復言、重諾，非信也；

translations.literal: repeated words and heavy promises—that is not true faith;
translations.idiomatic: endless vows and grand promises are not true faith;

sentences.zh: 糜金、散玉，非惠也；

translations.literal: scattering gold and jade—that is not true generosity;
translations.idiomatic: pouring out gold and jade is not true generosity;

translations.literal: cutting the throat and ripping the belly—that is not true courage.
translations.idiomatic: slitting the throat and ripping the belly is not true courage.

translations.literal: In sum, scheming without far sight and acting without righteousness—are they not of the same breed as Bai Gusheng of Chu!
translations.idiomatic: In the end, plans without foresight and deeds without righteousness—are they not kin to Bai Gusheng of Chu?

sentences.zh: ::荊軻懷其豢養之私，不顧七族，欲以尺八匕首強燕而弱秦，不亦愚乎！

translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong judged them thus: Yao Li was the spider's gossamer wasted; Nie Zheng, a brave man's life wasted; Jing Ke, an assassin's life wasted—none may be called righteous.

translations.literal: In this way Qi’s prestige may be established and the state of Qin destroyed—is it only to preserve one’s own state?”
translations.idiomatic: In this way Qi’s prestige can be restored and Qin destroyed—is that not better than merely preserving your own state?”

translations.literal: 1. Wang Ben attacked Qi from the south via Yan; in the end he entered Linzi, and none of the people dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Wang Ben attacked Qi from the south through Yan; he finally entered Linzi, and none of the people dared resist.

sentences.zh: 秦使人誘齊王，約封以五百里之地。

translations.literal: Qin sent men to entice the king of Qi, promising enfeoffment with five hundred li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Qin sent men to lure the king of Qi, promising him a fief of five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 齊王遂降，秦遷之共，處之松柏之間，餓而死。

translations.literal: The king of Qi thereupon surrendered; Qin moved him to Gong and placed him among pines and cypresses, where he starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi surrendered; Qin moved him to Gong, lodged him among pines and cypresses, and let him starve to death.

sentences.zh: 齊人怨王建不早與諸侯合從，聽奸人賓客以亡其國，歌之曰：「松耶，柏耶，住建共者客耶！

translations.literal: The people of Qi resented that King Jian had not early joined the feudal lords in the vertical alliance and had heeded treacherous guest-ministers to the ruin of their state; they sang: “Pine, eh? Cypress, eh? Was it the guest-ministers who lodged Jian at Gong!”
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi blamed King Jian for not joining the vertical alliance early and for heeding treacherous retainers until the state perished; they sang: “Pine, eh? Cypress, eh? Was it the retainers who put Jian at Gong!”

sentences.zh: 」疾建用客之不詳也。

translations.literal: ” They blamed Jian for employing guest-ministers without careful scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: ” They blamed Jian for employing retainers without due scrutiny.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：從衡之說雖反覆百端，然大要合從者，六國之利也。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: Though the doctrines of vertical and horizontal alliances twist and turn in a hundred ways, in sum the vertical alliance is to the benefit of the Six States.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: Though the theories of vertical and horizontal alliances twist a hundred ways, in essence the vertical alliance serves the Six States’ interest.

sentences.zh: 昔先王建萬國，親諸侯，使之朝聘以相交，饗宴以相樂，會盟以相結者，無他，欲其同心戮力以保國家也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Former Kings established the myriad states, treated the feudal lords as kin, and had them pay court and send envoys to communicate, feast and banquet to rejoice together, and meet in covenant to bind one another—there was no other purpose than to wish them united in heart and united in strength to preserve their states.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Former Kings founded the myriad states, treated the lords as kin, and had them exchange court visits and envoys, feast together, and covenant together—nothing more than wishing them united in heart and effort to preserve their states.

sentences.zh: 向使六國能以信義相親，則秦雖強暴，安得而亡之哉！

translations.literal: Had the Six States only been able to treat one another with trust and righteousness, then however violent Qin might have been, how could it have destroyed them!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Six States only treated one another with trust and righteousness, however brutal Qin was, how could it have destroyed them!

sentences.zh: 夫三晉者，齊、楚之籓蔽；

translations.literal: The Three Jin were screen and shield for Qi and Chu;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Jin were Qi and Chu’s screen and shield;

sentences.zh: 齊、楚者，三晉之根柢；

translations.literal: Qi and Chu were root and foundation for the Three Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chu were the Three Jin’s root and foundation;

sentences.zh: 形勢相資，表里相依。

translations.literal: their strategic positions complemented one another, outer and inner relying on each other.
translations.idiomatic: their strategic positions complemented one another; outer and inner relied on each other.

sentences.zh: 故以三晉而攻齊、楚，自絕其根柢也；

translations.literal: Hence to use the Three Jin to attack Qi and Chu was to cut off one’s own root and foundation;
translations.idiomatic: Hence to use the Three Jin to attack Qi and Chu was to cut off one’s own foundation;

sentences.zh: 以齊、楚而攻三晉，自撤其籓蔽也。

translations.literal: to use Qi and Chu to attack the Three Jin was to pull away one’s own screen and shield.
translations.idiomatic: to use Qi and Chu to attack the Three Jin was to pull away one’s own screen.

sentences.zh: 安有撤其籓蔽以媚盜，曰「盜將愛我而不攻」，豈不悖哉！

translations.literal: How could one pull away one’s screen and shield to court a thief, saying “The thief will love me and not attack”—is this not perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Who pulls away his screen to flatter a thief, saying “The thief will love me and not attack”—is that not absurd!

sentences.zh: 2王初并天下，自以為德兼三皇，功過五帝，乃更號曰「皇帝」，命為「制」，令為「詔」，自稱曰「朕」。

translations.literal: 2. When the king first united all under Heaven, he deemed his virtue embraced the Three August Ones and his merit surpassed the Five Emperors; he thereupon changed his title to “August Emperor,” styled his orders “ordinances,” his commands “edicts,” and called himself “I, the August One.”
translations.idiomatic: 2. When the king first united the realm, he thought his virtue matched the Three Sovereigns and his achievement surpassed the Five Emperors; he changed his title to “August Emperor,” called his orders “ordinances,” his commands “edicts,” and referred to himself as “I, the August One.”

sentences.zh: 追尊莊襄王為太上皇。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored King Zhuangxiang as Grand Supreme August One.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored King Zhuangxiang as Grand Supreme August One.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「死而以行為謚，則是子議父，臣議君也，甚無謂。

translations.literal: An ordinance said: “To give posthumous names based on conduct after death is for sons to judge fathers and ministers to judge their rulers—most pointless.
translations.idiomatic: An ordinance said: “To give posthumous titles based on conduct after death is for sons to judge fathers and ministers to judge rulers—utterly pointless.

sentences.zh: 自今以來，除謚法。

translations.literal: From this time forward, abolish the system of posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, abolish the system of posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 朕為始皇帝，後世以計數，二世、三世至于萬世，傳之無窮。

translations.literal: “I, the August One, am the First August Emperor; later ages shall count by number—Second, Third, on to ten thousand generations, transmitted without end.”
translations.idiomatic: “I am the First August Emperor; later ages shall count by number—Second, Third, on to ten thousand generations, transmitted without end.”

sentences.zh: 3初，齊威、宣之時，鄒衍論著終始五德之運；

translations.literal: 3. In the beginning, in the time of Kings Wei and Xuan of Qi, Zou Yan wrote on the cycles of the Five Powers from beginning to end;
translations.idiomatic: 3. Early on, in the time of Kings Wei and Xuan of Qi, Zou Yan wrote on the cyclical course of the Five Powers;

sentences.zh: 及始皇并天下，齊人奏之。

translations.literal: when the First August Emperor united all under Heaven, men of Qi presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: when the First August Emperor united the realm, men of Qi presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 始皇採用其說，以為周得火德，秦代周，從所不勝，為水德。

translations.literal: The First August Emperor adopted the doctrine, holding that Zhou had obtained the power of Fire; Qin supplanted Zhou, following what overcomes the other, and took the power of Water.
translations.idiomatic: The First August Emperor adopted it, holding that Zhou had the power of Fire, Qin replaced Zhou by following what overcomes Fire, and took the power of Water.

sentences.zh: 始改年，朝賀皆自十月朔；

translations.literal: He began by changing the year-count; court audiences and congratulations all started from the first day of the tenth month;
translations.idiomatic: He changed the calendar year; court audiences and congratulations all began on the first day of the tenth month;

sentences.zh: 衣服、旌旄、節旗皆尚黑，數以六為紀。

translations.literal: garments, banners, pennants, and insignia all honored black; numbers took six as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: garments, banners, pennants, and standards all honored black; numbers took six as their standard.

translations.literal: The court administrator Li Si said: “The sons and younger brothers of the same surname whom Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou enfeoffed were very numerous; later, when kin grew distant, they attacked one another like mortal enemies, and the Son of Heaven of Zhou could not forbid it.

translations.literal: Now within the seas all rely on Your Majesty’s numinous power in unification; all are transformed into commanderies and counties; sons and merit-officers may be heavily rewarded with public taxes and levies—they are very easy to control, and when the realm has no divergent intent, this is the method of tranquillity.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm relies on Your Majesty’s numinous power in unification; all are commanderies and counties; sons and meritorious ministers can be richly rewarded from public taxes—they are easy to control, and when the realm has no other intent, this is the way to peace.

translations.literal: To install feudal lords would be inexpedient.”
translations.idiomatic: Installing feudal lords would be inexpedient.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇曰：「天下共苦戰鬥不休，以有侯王。

translations.literal: ” The First August Emperor said: “All under Heaven together suffered from unceasing warfare because there were marquises and kings.
translations.idiomatic: ” The First August Emperor said: “All under Heaven suffered endless warfare because there were marquises and kings.

sentences.zh: 賴宗廟，天下初定，又復立國，是樹兵也；

translations.literal: Relying on the ancestral temple, when the realm was first settled, to establish states again would be to plant arms;
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the ancestral temple, the realm is newly settled; to establish states again would be to plant arms;

sentences.zh: 而求其寧息，豈不難哉！

translations.literal: and to seek their tranquillity and rest—would this not be difficult!
translations.idiomatic: and to seek peace from that—would that not be hard!

sentences.zh: 廷尉議是。

translations.literal: The court administrator’s proposal is correct.”
translations.idiomatic: The court administrator’s proposal is correct.”

sentences.zh: 分天下為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監。

translations.literal: The realm was divided into thirty-six commanderies; each commandery had a governor, military commandant, and inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was divided into thirty-six commanderies; each commandery had a governor, military commandant, and inspector.

sentences.zh: 收天下兵聚咸陽，銷以為鍾鐻、金人十二，重各千石，置宮廷中。

translations.literal: Weapons from all under Heaven were collected at Xianyang, melted to cast bells, bell-stands, and twelve golden figures, each weighing a thousand piculs, and set within the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons from across the realm were collected at Xianyang, melted into bells, bell-stands, and twelve golden figures, each weighing a thousand piculs, and placed in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 一法度、衡、石、丈尺。

translations.literal: Standards of measure, balance, weight, and yardstick were unified.
translations.idiomatic: Standards of measure, weights, and dimensions were unified.

sentences.zh: 徙天下豪傑於咸陽十二萬戶。

translations.literal: The powerful families of all under Heaven were moved to Xianyang—one hundred twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful families of the realm were moved to Xianyang—one hundred twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諸廟及章臺、上林皆在渭南。

translations.literal: The various temples together with Zhang Terrace and the Upper Park were all south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The temples, Zhang Terrace, and the Upper Park were all south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 每破諸侯，寫放其宮室，作之咸陽北阪上，南臨渭，自雍門以東至涇、渭，殿屋、覆道、周閣相屬，所得諸侯美人、鐘鼓以充入之。

translations.literal: Each time feudal lords were overthrown, their palaces were copied and erected on the north slope at Xianyang, facing south over the Wei; from Yong Gate eastward to the Jing and Wei rivers, halls, covered ways, and encircling galleries linked one to another; captured ladies of the feudal lords, bells and drums were installed to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a feudal state fell, its palaces were copied and built on the north slope at Xianyang, facing south over the Wei; from Yong Gate east to the Jing and Wei, halls, covered ways, and encircling galleries ran in succession; captured ladies, bells, and drums filled them.

sentences.zh: 1始皇巡隴西、北地，至雞頭山，過回中焉。

translations.literal: 1. The First August Emperor toured Longxi and Beidi, reached Mount Jitou, and passed through Huizhong.
translations.idiomatic: 1. The First August Emperor toured Longxi and Beidi, reached Mount Jitou, and passed through Huizhong.

sentences.zh: 2作信宮渭南，已，更命曰極廟。

translations.literal: 2. He built the Trust Palace south of the Wei; when finished, he renamed it the Ultimate Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 2. He built the Trust Palace south of the Wei; when it was finished, he renamed it the Ultimate Temple.

sentences.zh: 自極廟道通驪山，作甘泉前殿，築甬道自咸陽屬之，治馳道於天下。

translations.literal: From the Ultimate Temple a road was opened through to Mount Li; the front hall of Ganquan was built; a covered roadway was constructed from Xianyang connecting to it; express roads were engineered throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ultimate Temple a road ran through to Mount Li; the front hall of Ganquan was built; a covered roadway was constructed from Xianyang to connect with it; express roads were built throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 1始皇東行郡、縣，上鄒嶧山，立石頌功業。

translations.literal: 1. The First August Emperor traveled east through the commanderies and counties, ascended Mount Yi of Zou, and erected a stone praising his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: 1. The First August Emperor traveled east through the commanderies and counties, ascended Mount Yi at Zou, and erected a stone praising his achievements.

sentences.zh: 於是召集魯儒生七十人，至泰山下，議封禪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned seventy Confucian scholars of Lu to the foot of Mount Tai to deliberate on the feng and shan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he summoned seventy Confucian scholars of Lu to the foot of Mount Tai to discuss the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 諸儒或曰：「古者封禪，為蒲車，惡傷山之土石、草木；

translations.literal: Some of the scholars said: “In antiquity for the feng and shan sacrifices they used carts of rushes, loathing to injure the mountain’s earth, stones, and vegetation;
translations.idiomatic: Some scholars said: “In antiquity for the feng and shan rites they used rush carts, loathing to harm the mountain’s earth, stone, and plants;

sentences.zh: 掃地而祭，席用菹秸。

translations.literal: they swept the ground to sacrifice, and mats were of chopped straw.”
translations.idiomatic: they swept the ground to sacrifice, and mats were of chopped straw.”

sentences.zh: 」議各乖異。

translations.literal: ” The proposals each differed and conflicted.
translations.idiomatic: ” Their proposals all differed.

sentences.zh: 始皇以其難施用，由此絀儒生。

translations.literal: The First August Emperor deemed them hard to apply; from this he rebuffed the scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The First August Emperor found them impractical and from this rebuffed the scholars.

sentences.zh: 而遂除車道，上自泰山陽至顛，立石頌德；

translations.literal: He then cleared the carriage road, ascended from the southern face of Mount Tai to the summit, erected a stone praising his virtue;
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the carriage road, ascended from the southern face of Mount Tai to the summit, and erected a stone praising his virtue;

sentences.zh: 從陰道下，禪於梁父。

translations.literal: descended by the shady path, and performed the shan rite at Mount Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: descended by the northern path and performed the shan rite at Mount Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 其禮頗采太祝之祀雍上帝所用，而封藏皆秘之，世不得而記也。

translations.literal: The rites largely adopted what the grand invoker used in sacrificing to the Supreme God at Yong, but what was sealed and stored was all kept secret, and the age has no record of it.
translations.idiomatic: The rites largely followed what the grand invoker used in sacrificing to the Supreme God at Yong, but what was sealed and stored was kept secret, and later ages have no record of it.

sentences.zh: 於是始皇遂東遊海上，行禮祠名山、大川及八神。

translations.literal: Thereupon the First August Emperor traveled east along the sea, performing rites and sacrificing to famous mountains, great rivers, and the Eight Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the First August Emperor traveled east along the coast, performing rites and sacrificing to famous mountains, great rivers, and the Eight Spirits.

sentences.zh: 始皇南登琅邪，大樂之，留三月，作琅邪臺，立石頌德，明得意。

translations.literal: The First August Emperor ascended Langye in the south, greatly delighted in it, stayed three months, built the Langye Terrace, erected a stone praising his virtue, making clear his satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: The First August Emperor ascended Langye in the south, greatly delighted in it, stayed three months, built the Langye Terrace, erected a stone praising his virtue, showing his satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 初，燕人宋毋忌、羨門子高之徒稱有仙道、形解銷化之術，燕、齊迂怪之士皆爭傳習之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, men of Yan such as Master Wuji of Song, Master Zigaoshan, and their like claimed techniques of the Way of immortals and of dissolving the body and melting away; eccentric and strange gentlemen of Yan and Qi all vied to transmit and study them.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, men of Yan such as Master Wuji of Song and Master Zigaoshan claimed the Way of immortals and techniques of bodily dissolution and transmutation; eccentric gentlemen of Yan and Qi all vied to transmit and study them.

sentences.zh: 自齊威王、宣王、燕昭王皆信其言，使人入海求蓬萊、方丈、瀛洲，雲此三神山在勃海中，去人不遠。

translations.literal: From King Wei and King Xuan of Qi and King Zhao of Yan, all believed their words and sent men to sea seeking Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou—it was said these three spirit-isles were in the Bohai Sea, not far from men.
translations.idiomatic: From Kings Wei and Xuan of Qi and King Zhao of Yan, all believed them and sent men to sea seeking Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou—it was said these three spirit-isles lay in the Bohai Sea, not far from mankind.

sentences.zh: 患且至，則風引舡去。

translations.literal: When trouble was about to arrive, a wind would draw the boats away.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to arrive, a wind would carry the boats away.

sentences.zh: 嘗有至者，諸仙人及不死之藥皆在焉。

translations.literal: Some had reached them; all the immortals and the elixir of deathlessness were there.
translations.idiomatic: Some had reached them; the immortals and the elixir of immortality were all there.

sentences.zh: 及始皇至海上，諸方士齊人徐市等爭上書言之，請得齊戒與童男女求之。

translations.literal: When the First August Emperor reached the sea, various masters of the arts, such as Xu Shi of Qi, all vied to memorialize on the matter, asking to obtain purification by fasting and boys and girls to go seek them.
translations.idiomatic: When the First August Emperor reached the coast, various masters of the arts such as Xu Shi of Qi all vied to memorialize on the matter, asking for purification by fasting and boys and girls to seek them.

sentences.zh: 於是遣徐市發童男女數千人入海求之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Xu Shi, dispatching several thousand boys and girls to sea to seek them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent Xu Shi with several thousand boys and girls to sea to seek them.

sentences.zh: 舡交海中，皆以風解，曰：「未能至，望見之焉。

translations.literal: The boats met in mid-sea; all were dispersed by wind; they said: “We could not reach them, yet we caught sight of them from afar.”
translations.idiomatic: The boats met at sea; all were scattered by wind; they said: “We could not reach them, yet we saw them from afar.”

sentences.zh: 始皇還，過彭城，齋戒禱祠，欲出周鼎泗水，使千人沒水求之，弗得。

translations.literal: The First August Emperor returned, passed Pengcheng, fasted in purification and prayed and sacrificed, wished to raise the cauldrons of Zhou from the Si River, sent a thousand men to dive into the water seeking them, but did not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: The First August Emperor returned, passed Pengcheng, purified himself by fasting and prayed and sacrificed, wished to raise the Zhou cauldrons from the Si River, sent a thousand men diving to seek them, but did not obtain them.

sentences.zh: 乃西南渡淮水，之衡山、南郡。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Huai southwestward, going to Hengshan and Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the Huai southwestward, going to Hengshan and Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 浮江至湘山祠，逢大風，幾不能渡。

translations.literal: He floated down the river to the shrine of Mount Xiang, met a great wind, and was nearly unable to cross.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed down the river to the shrine of Mount Xiang, met a great gale, and was nearly unable to cross.

sentences.zh: 上問博士曰：「湘君何神？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the erudites, saying: “What god is the Lord of the Xiang?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the erudites: “What deity is the Lord of the Xiang?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聞之：堯女，舜之妻，葬此。

translations.literal: ” One replied: “I have heard: a daughter of Yao, wife of Shun, is buried here.
translations.idiomatic: ” One replied: “I have heard it said: a daughter of Yao, wife of Shun, is buried here.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇大怒，使刑徒三千人皆伐湘山樹，赭其山。

translations.literal: ” The First Emperor was greatly angered and sent three thousand convict laborers all to fell the trees of Mount Xiang and made the mountain red.
translations.idiomatic: ” The First Emperor was furious and sent three thousand convict laborers to fell every tree on Mount Xiang and redden the mountain.

sentences.zh: 遂自南郡由武關歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon returned from Nan commandery by way of Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned from Nan commandery by way of Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 2初，韓人張良，其父、祖以上五世相韓。

translations.literal: 2. Earlier, Zhang Liang of Han—his father, grandfather, and ancestors above for five generations had been chancellors of Han.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Earlier, Zhang Liang of Han came from a family that had served as chancellor of Han for five generations, from his father and grandfather back.

sentences.zh: 及韓亡，良散千金之產，欲為韓報仇。

translations.literal: When Han perished, Liang dispersed an estate worth a thousand in gold, wishing to avenge Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fell, Liang gave away an estate worth a thousand in gold, seeking to avenge Han.

sentences.zh: 1始皇東遊，至陽武博浪沙中，張良令力士操鐵椎狙擊始皇，誤中副車。

translations.literal: 1. The First Emperor toured east, reaching Bolang Sand in Yangwu; Zhang Liang had a strongman wield an iron mace and lie in ambush to strike the First Emperor, but he mistakenly hit the secondary carriage.
translations.idiomatic: 1. On an eastern tour the First Emperor reached Bolang Sand in Yangwu; Zhang Liang had a strongman wield an iron mace in ambush, but the blow struck the secondary carriage by mistake.

sentences.zh: 始皇驚，求，弗得；

translations.literal: The First Emperor was alarmed, searched, and did not find him;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor was alarmed and searched, but could not find him;

sentences.zh: 令天下大索十日。

translations.literal: he ordered a great search throughout the realm for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered a realm-wide manhunt for ten days.

sentences.zh: 2始皇遂登之罘，刻石；

translations.literal: 2. The First Emperor thereupon ascended Zhi, carved a stone;
translations.idiomatic: 2. The First Emperor then ascended Zhi and had a stone inscribed;

sentences.zh: 旋，之琅邪，道上黨入。

translations.literal: soon after went to Langye, and on the road entered from Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: then went on to Langye and entered by way of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 1使黔首自實田。

translations.literal: 1. He had the black-headed people register their own fields.
translations.idiomatic: 1. He ordered commoners to register their own land holdings.

sentences.zh: 1始皇之碣石，使燕人盧生求羨門，刻碣石門。

translations.literal: 1. The First Emperor went to Jieshi, sent the man of Yan Lu Sheng to seek Xianmen, and carved the Jieshi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: 1. The First Emperor went to Jieshi, sent Lu Sheng of Yan to seek Xianmen, and had the Jieshi Gate inscribed.

sentences.zh: 壞城郭，決通堤坊。

translations.literal: He destroyed city walls and ramparts and opened and cleared dikes and embankments.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down outer walls and ramparts and cut through dikes and embankments to open waterways.

sentences.zh: 始皇巡北邊，從上郡入。

translations.literal: The First Emperor inspected the northern border and entered by way of Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor toured the northern frontier and entered through Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 盧生使入海還，因奏《錄圖書》曰：「亡秦者胡也。

translations.literal: Lu Sheng, sent on a mission to the sea, returned and thereupon presented the Recorded Chart Book, saying: “He who will destroy Qin is Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sheng returned from a mission to the sea and presented the Recorded Chart Book, saying: “He who will destroy Qin is Hu.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇乃遣將軍蒙恬發兵三十萬人，北伐匈奴。

translations.literal: ” The First Emperor thereupon sent the general Meng Tian to raise an army of three hundred thousand men and march north to attack the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: ” The First Emperor then sent General Meng Tian with an army of three hundred thousand to attack the Xiongnu in the north.

sentences.zh: 1發諸嘗逋亡人、贅婿、賈人為兵，略取南越陸梁地，置桂林、南海、象郡；

translations.literal: 1. He drafted as soldiers all who had ever fled as fugitives, surplus sons-in-law, and merchants, seized the Luliang lands of Southern Yue, and established the commanderies of Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: 1. He drafted fugitives, surplus sons-in-law, and merchants as soldiers, seized the Luliang region of Southern Yue, and established the commanderies of Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang;

sentences.zh: 以謫徙民五十萬人戍五嶺，與越雜處。

translations.literal: he sent five hundred thousand banished and relocated people to garrison the Five Ridges, living mixed among the Yue.
translations.idiomatic: and sent five hundred thousand exiles to garrison the Five Ridges, living intermingled with the Yue.

sentences.zh: 2蒙恬斥逐匈奴，收河南地為四十四縣。

translations.literal: 2. Meng Tian drove off the Xiongnu, recovered the lands south of the River, and made them into forty-four counties.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Meng Tian drove back the Xiongnu, recovered the territory south of the Yellow River, and organized it into forty-four counties.

sentences.zh: 築長城，因地形，用制險塞。

translations.literal: He built the Long Wall, following the terrain, using it to control strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Long Wall along the terrain to control strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 起臨洮至遼東，延袤萬餘里。

translations.literal: It ran from Lintao to Liaodong, extending more than ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It ran from Lintao to Liaodong, more than ten thousand li end to end.

sentences.zh: 於是渡河，據陽山，逶迤而北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed the river, held Yang Mountain, and wound northward.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river, held Yang Mountain, and wound his way north.

sentences.zh: 暴師於外十餘年。

translations.literal: He exposed his army in the field for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His army remained in the field for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 蒙恬常居上郡統治之，威振匈奴。

translations.literal: Meng Tian constantly resided in Shang commandery governing it, and his awesomeness shook the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tian usually stayed in Shang commandery to govern the region, and his prestige awed the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 1謫治獄吏不直及覆獄故、失者，築長城及處南越地。

translations.literal: 1. Those sentenced for prison officers’ lack of rectitude and for retrying old cases and failures were banished to build the Long Wall and serve in the Southern Yue region.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Officials convicted of judicial misconduct or of retrying closed cases were banished to build the Long Wall or serve in the Southern Yue lands.

sentences.zh: 丞相李斯上書曰：「異時諸侯並爭，厚招遊學。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Si submitted a memorial, saying: “In former times the feudal lords contended together and lavishly recruited wandering scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Si memorialized the throne: “In former times the feudal lords fought one another and lavishly recruited wandering scholars.”

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，法令出一，百姓當家則力農工，士則學習法令。

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled, laws and orders issue from one source; common people when at home should exert themselves in farming and crafts, and gentlemen should study laws and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is settled and laws issue from a single source: commoners at home should devote themselves to farming and crafts, and gentlemen should study the laws.”

sentences.zh: 今諸生不師今而學古，以非當世，惑亂黔首，相與非法教。

translations.literal: Now the various scholars do not take the present as teacher but study antiquity, using it to condemn the age, bewilder and disorder the black-headed people, and band together against the lawful teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scholars today ignore the present to study antiquity, condemn the age, mislead the common people, and band together against lawful instruction.”

sentences.zh: 人聞令下，則各以其學議之，入則心非，出則巷議，誇主以為名，異趣以為高，率群下以造謗。

translations.literal: When men hear an order issued, each discusses it with his own learning; inwardly they secretly disapprove, outwardly they debate in the lanes, praise the ruler to make a name, take strange pursuits as loftiness, and lead the masses below to manufacture slander.
translations.idiomatic: When an order is issued, each debates it by his own school; inwardly they disapprove, outwardly they gossip in the streets, flatter the ruler for reputation, prize eccentric views as superiority, and lead the masses to slander.”

sentences.zh: 如此弗禁，則主勢降乎上，黨與成乎下。

translations.literal: If this is not forbidden, then the ruler’s authority will sink above and factions will form below.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not stopped, the ruler’s authority will decline above and factions will form below.”

sentences.zh: 禁之便！

translations.literal: To forbid it is expedient!
translations.idiomatic: It must be forbidden!”

sentences.zh: 臣請史官非秦記皆燒之；

translations.literal: Your servant requests that all records in the historians’ offices that are not Qin annals be burned;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all records in the historians’ offices that are not Qin annals be burned;

sentences.zh: 非博士官所職，天下有藏《詩》、《書》、百家語者，皆詣守、尉雜燒之。

translations.literal: apart from those in the charge of erudite officials, wherever under Heaven there are stored the Odes, the Documents, or the sayings of the hundred schools, all are to be brought to the governor and commandant to be burned in a mixed heap.
translations.idiomatic: and that all copies of the Odes, Documents, and writings of the hundred schools held outside erudite offices be brought to local governors and commandants and burned.

sentences.zh: 有敢偶語《詩》、《書》，棄市；

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak together of the Odes or Documents—execution in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares discuss the Odes or Documents together shall be executed in the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 以古非今者族；

translations.literal: whoever uses antiquity to condemn the present—clan extermination;
translations.idiomatic: whoever uses antiquity to condemn the present shall have his clan exterminated;

sentences.zh: 吏見知不舉，與同罪。

translations.literal: an official who sees and knows but does not report shares the same crime.
translations.idiomatic: and any official who sees this and fails to report it shares the same punishment.”

sentences.zh: 令下三十日，不燒，黔為城旦。

translations.literal: Thirty days after the order is issued, those who have not burned their books are tattooed and made dawn-wall laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty days after the order, those who have not burned their books shall be tattooed and sentenced to dawn-wall labor.”

sentences.zh: 所不去者，醫藥、卜筮、種樹之書。

translations.literal: What is not to be removed: books on medicine, divination, and planting.
translations.idiomatic: Books on medicine, divination, and agriculture are exempt.”

sentences.zh: 若有欲學法令者，以吏為師。

translations.literal: If there are those who wish to study laws and orders, let officials be their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to study laws and orders must take officials as their teachers.”

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: ” An edict said: “Approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” The edict read: “Approved.”

sentences.zh: 魏人陳餘謂孔鮒曰：「秦將滅先王之籍，而子為書籍之主，其危哉！

translations.literal: Chen Yu of Wei said to Kong Fu: “Qin is about to destroy the records of the former kings, and you, sir, are master of the books—how perilous!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu of Wei said to Kong Fu: “Qin is about to destroy the records of the former kings, and you are keeper of the books—how dangerous!”

sentences.zh: 」子魚曰：「吾為無用之學，知吾者惟友。

translations.literal: ” Ziyu said: “My learning is useless; only friends know me.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ziyu said: “My learning is useless; only friends know me.”

sentences.zh: 秦非吾友，吾何危哉！

translations.literal: Qin is not my friend—why should I be in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Qin is not my friend—why should I be in peril?”

sentences.zh: 吾將藏之以待其求；

translations.literal: I shall hide them and wait for Qin to seek them;
translations.idiomatic: I shall hide them and wait until they are sought;

sentences.zh: 求至，無患矣。

translations.literal: when the seeking comes, there will be no worry.
translations.idiomatic: once they are sought, there will be no trouble.”

sentences.zh: 1使蒙恬除直道，道九原，抵雲陽，塹山堙谷千八百里，數年不就。

translations.literal: 1. He had Meng Tian clear the Straight Road, road through Jiuyuan, reach Yunyang, cut through mountains and fill valleys for one thousand eight hundred li—several years without completion.
translations.idiomatic: 1. He had Meng Tian clear the Straight Road from Jiuyuan to Yunyang, cutting through mountains and filling valleys for eighteen hundred li; it was still unfinished after several years.

sentences.zh: 2始皇以為咸陽人多，先王之宮廷小，乃營作朝宮渭南上林苑中，先作前殿阿房，東西五百步，南北五十丈，上可以坐萬人，下可以建五丈旗，周馳為閣道，自殿下直抵南山，表南山之顛以為闕。

translations.literal: 2. The First Emperor thought the people of Xianyang numerous and the former kings’ palaces small; he thereupon built the court palace in the Shanglin Park south of the Wei in Xianyang, first constructing the front hall of Epang—five hundred paces east to west, five hundred zhang north to south, above able to seat ten thousand men, below able to raise a five-zhang banner; all around he ran elevated corridors, from beneath the hall straight to South Mountain, marking the summit of South Mountain as the gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Thinking Xianyang overcrowded and the former kings’ palaces too small, he built a court palace in the Shanglin Park south of the Wei, first erecting the front hall of Epang—five hundred paces east to west and five hundred zhang north to south, able to seat ten thousand above and fly a fifty-foot banner below; elevated corridors ran all around from the hall straight to South Mountain, whose summit was marked as a gate-tower.

sentences.zh: 為衣覆道，自阿房渡渭，屬之咸陽，以象天極閣道、絕漢抵營室也。

translations.literal: He made covered passageways, crossing the Wei from Epang and linking to Xianyang, to symbolize the Celestial Pole’s elevated corridor crossing the Milky Way to reach the Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: He built covered passageways from Epang across the Wei to link with Xianyang, symbolizing the celestial pole’s elevated corridor crossing the Milky Way to the Encampment constellation.

sentences.zh: 隱宮、徒刑者七十〔餘〕萬人<ref>隱宮徒刑者七十〔餘〕萬人據章校補。

translations.literal: Hidden-palace workers and convict laborers numbered seven hundred thousand and more〔餘〕<ref>Hidden-palace workers and convict laborers seven hundred thousand and more〔餘〕—supplemented according to Zhang’s collation.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden-palace workers and convict laborers numbered seven hundred thousand and more〔餘〕<ref>Hidden-palace workers and convict laborers seven hundred thousand and more〔餘〕—supplemented per Zhang’s collation.

sentences.zh: </ref>，乃分作阿房宮或作驪山。

translations.literal: </ref>, and they were then divided between building Epang Palace or building Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, and they were divided between building Epang Palace and building Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 發北山石槨，寫蜀、荊地材，皆至；

translations.literal: He sent men to quarry stone coffin-blocks in the northern mountains and transport timber from Shu and Jing lands—all arrived;
translations.idiomatic: Stone was quarried in the northern mountains and timber floated from Shu and Jing—all arrived;

sentences.zh: 關中計宮三百，關外四百餘。

translations.literal: within the passes the palaces numbered three hundred; outside the passes, more than four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: within the passes there were three hundred palaces; outside, more than four hundred.

sentences.zh: 於是立石東海上朐界中，以為秦東門。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up a stone in the boundary of Ju on the eastern sea, taking it as Qin’s eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then set up a stone at Ju on the eastern sea as Qin’s eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 因徙三萬家驪邑，五萬家雲陽，皆復不事十歲。

translations.literal: He thereupon moved thirty thousand households to Li Yi and fifty thousand households to Yunyang, all exempted from labor and service for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He moved thirty thousand households to Li Yi and fifty thousand to Yunyang, all exempt from taxes and corvée for ten years.

sentences.zh: 盧生說始皇曰：「方中：人主時為微行以辟惡鬼。

translations.literal: Lu Sheng urged the First Emperor, saying: “Among the methods: the ruler should at times make discreet journeys to avoid evil ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sheng urged the First Emperor: “By one method, the ruler should sometimes travel incognito to avoid evil ghosts.”

sentences.zh: 惡鬼辟，真人至。

translations.literal: When evil ghosts are avoided, the True Man arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When evil ghosts are kept away, the True Man will come.”

sentences.zh: 願上所居宮毋令人知，然後不死之藥殆可得也。

translations.literal: I wish that where Your Majesty dwells in palaces no one may know—then the elixir of immortality may nearly be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If no one knows where Your Majesty lodges, the elixir of immortality may almost be obtained.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇曰：「吾慕真人。

translations.literal: ” The First Emperor said: “I admire the True Man.
translations.idiomatic: ” The First Emperor said: “I admire the True Man.”

sentences.zh: 」自謂「真人」，不稱「朕」。

translations.literal: ” He called himself “True Man” and did not use the title “I, the Emperor.”
translations.idiomatic: ” He called himself “True Man” and stopped using the title zhen (“I, the Emperor”).

sentences.zh: 乃令咸陽之旁二百里內宮觀二百七十，複道、甬道相連，帷帳、鐘鼓、美人充之，各案署不移徙。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered two hundred and seventy palaces and towers within two hundred li of Xianyang, linked by elevated corridors and covered walkways, filled with curtains, bells and drums, and beauties, each with its office fixed without removal.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered two hundred and seventy palaces and towers within two hundred li of Xianyang, linked by elevated and covered walkways and stocked with hangings, bells, drums, and consorts, each with fixed staff that never moved.

sentences.zh: 行所幸，有言其處者，罪死。

translations.literal: Wherever he traveled on his progresses, whoever spoke of the place—death as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever revealed where he was traveling was put to death.

sentences.zh: 始皇幸梁山宮，從山上見丞相車騎眾，弗善也。

translations.literal: The First Emperor favored Liang Mountain Palace; from the mountain he saw the chancellor’s chariots and horsemen numerous and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang Mountain Palace the First Emperor looked down from the hill, saw the chancellor’s large retinue of chariots and horsemen, and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 中人或告丞相，丞相後損車騎。

translations.literal: A palace attendant told the chancellor, and afterward the chancellor reduced his chariots and horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant told the chancellor, who thereafter reduced his escort.

sentences.zh: 始皇怒曰：「此中人泄吾語！

translations.literal: The First Emperor said angrily: “These palace people leaked my words!
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor raged: “These palace people leaked my words!”

sentences.zh: 」案問，莫服，捕時在旁者，盡殺之。

translations.literal: ” He investigated by interrogation; none confessed, so he seized those who had been present at the time and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: ” He investigated; none confessed, so he seized everyone who had been nearby and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 自是後，莫知行之所在。

translations.literal: From this time on, none knew where he was traveling.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one knew where he was.

sentences.zh: 群臣受決事者，悉於咸陽宮。

translations.literal: All ministers who received decisions on affairs were entirely at Xianyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers awaiting decisions all remained at Xianyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 侯生、盧生相與譏議始皇，因亡去。

translations.literal: Hou Sheng and Lu Sheng together ridiculed and criticized the First Emperor, and thereupon fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sheng and Lu Sheng mocked the First Emperor together and fled.

sentences.zh: 始皇聞之，大怒曰：「盧生等，吾尊賜之甚厚，今乃誹謗我！

translations.literal: The First Emperor heard of it and said in great anger: “Lu Sheng and the rest—I honored and rewarded them very richly, yet now they slander me!
translations.idiomatic: When he heard this, the First Emperor raged: “Lu Sheng and the rest—I honored and enriched them lavishly, yet now they slander me!”

sentences.zh: 諸生在咸陽者，吾使人廉問，或為妖言以亂黔首。

translations.literal: As for the various scholars in Xianyang, I have sent men to investigate; some have made demonic talk to disorder the black-headed people.
translations.idiomatic: I have had the scholars in Xianyang investigated; some spread weird talk to confuse the people.”

sentences.zh: 」於是御史悉案問諸生。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the imperial censor fully investigated and interrogated the various scholars.
translations.idiomatic: ” The imperial censor then interrogated every scholar.

sentences.zh: 諸生傳相告引，乃自除犯禁者四百六十餘人，皆坑之咸陽，使天下知之，以懲後；

translations.literal: The scholars passed word to one another and implicated one another; those who had themselves eliminated offenders of the ban numbered more than four hundred and sixty—all were buried alive at Xianyang, to let the realm know and warn those after;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars informed on one another; more than four hundred and sixty who had violated the ban were identified and buried alive at Xianyang, so the realm would know and take warning;

sentences.zh: 益發謫徙邊。

translations.literal: banished exiles to the frontier were increased still more.
translations.idiomatic: and still more exiles were sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 始皇長子扶蘇諫曰：「諸生皆誦法孔子。

translations.literal: Fusu, the First Emperor’s eldest son, remonstrated, saying: “The various scholars all recite the laws of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Fusu, the First Emperor’s eldest son, remonstrated: “These scholars all study the laws of Confucius.”

sentences.zh: 今上皆重法繩之，臣恐天下不安。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty binds them all with heavy punishments; your servant fears the realm will not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty punishes them all harshly; I fear the realm will not be at peace.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇怒，使扶蘇北監蒙恬軍於上郡。

translations.literal: ” The First Emperor was angry and sent Fusu north to oversee Meng Tian’s army in Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: ” The First Emperor was angry and sent Fusu north to oversee Meng Tian’s army in Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 1有隕石于東郡。

translations.literal: 1. A meteorite fell in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 1. A meteorite fell in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 或刻其石曰：「始皇死而地分。

translations.literal: Someone carved on the stone, saying: “When the First Emperor dies, the land will divide.
translations.idiomatic: Someone carved on the stone: “When the First Emperor dies, the land will be divided.”

sentences.zh: 」始皇使御史逐問，莫服；

translations.literal: ” The First Emperor sent censors to pursue and question; none confessed;
translations.idiomatic: ” The First Emperor sent censors to investigate; none confessed;

sentences.zh: 盡取石旁居人誅之，燔其石。

translations.literal: he took all the residents beside the stone and executed them, and burned the stone.
translations.idiomatic: he executed everyone living near the stone and burned it.

sentences.zh: 2遷河北榆中三萬家；

translations.literal: 2. He moved thirty thousand households to Yuzhong north of the River;
translations.idiomatic: 2. He moved thirty thousand households to Yuzhong north of the Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 賜爵一級。

translations.literal: each was granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: each granted one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，癸丑，始皇出遊；

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, on the day guichou, the First Emperor set out on tour;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, on the day guichou, the First Emperor set out on tour;

sentences.zh: 左丞相李斯從，右丞相馮去疾守。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Li Si followed; Right Chancellor Feng Quji remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Li Si accompanied him; Right Chancellor Feng Quji stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 始皇二十餘子，少子胡亥最愛，請從；

translations.literal: The First Emperor had more than twenty sons; the youngest son Huhai was most beloved and asked to follow;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor had more than twenty sons; his youngest, Huhai, whom he loved most, asked to accompany him;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 2十一月，行至雲夢，望祀虞舜於九疑山。

translations.literal: 2. In the eleventh month he reached Yunmeng and made a distant sacrifice to Shun of Yu at Mount Jiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In the eleventh month he reached Yunmeng and offered a distant sacrifice to Emperor Shun at Mount Jiuyi.

sentences.zh: 浮江下，觀藉柯，渡海渚，過丹陽，至錢唐，臨浙江。

translations.literal: He floated down the river, viewed Jieke, crossed Haizhu, passed Danyang, reached Qiantang, and came to the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed downriver, viewed Jieke, crossed Haizhu, passed Danyang, reached Qiantang, and came to the Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 水波惡，乃西百二十里，從陿中渡。

translations.literal: The water’s waves were fierce, so he went west one hundred and twenty li and crossed from within the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The waves were too rough, so he went west a hundred and twenty li and crossed through the narrow pass.

sentences.zh: 上會稽，祭大禹，望于南海；

translations.literal: He ascended Kuaiji, sacrificed to Yu the Great, and gazed toward the southern sea;
translations.idiomatic: He ascended Mount Kuaiji, sacrificed to Yu the Great, and gazed toward the southern sea;

sentences.zh: 立石頌德。

translations.literal: he set up a stone praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: and set up a stone praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 還，過吳，從江乘渡。

translations.literal: On the return he passed Wu and crossed from Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he passed Wu and crossed from Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 並海上，北至琅邪、罘。

translations.literal: He followed the seacoast north to Langye and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the coast north to Langye and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 見巨魚，射殺之。

translations.literal: He saw a huge fish and shot and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: He saw an enormous fish and shot it dead.

sentences.zh: 遂並海西，至平原津而病。

translations.literal: He thereupon followed the western sea, reached Pingyuan Ford, and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He continued along the western coast to Pingyuan Ford, where he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 始皇惡言死，群臣莫敢言死事。

translations.literal: The First Emperor hated the word “death”; none of the ministers dared speak of death.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor hated any talk of death; no minister dared mention it.

sentences.zh: 病益甚，乃令中軍府令行符璽事趙高為書賜扶蘇曰：「與喪，會咸陽而葬。

translations.literal: As his illness grew worse, he ordered Zhao Gao, chief of the central army office who handled the tallies and seals, to write a letter bestowed on Fusu, saying: “Attend the funeral; meet at Xianyang for burial.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew worse, he had Zhao Gao, chief of the central army office who handled seals and tallies, write a letter to Fusu: “Attend the funeral and meet at Xianyang for burial.”

sentences.zh: 」書已封，在趙高所，未付使者。

translations.literal: ” The letter was already sealed and remained with Zhao Gao; it had not yet been given to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: ” The letter was sealed and remained with Zhao Gao; it had not yet been given to the messenger.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅<ref>丙寅此年七月丙子朔，無丙寅，或為丙申之誤。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, bingyin<ref>On bingyin: this year's seventh month had bingzi as the first day of the month; there was no bingyin—or it may be an error for bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, bingyin<ref>On bingyin: that year's seventh month began on bingzi; there was no bingyin—or the day may be an error for bingshen.

sentences.zh: </ref>，始皇崩於沙丘平臺。

translations.literal: </ref> the First Emperor died at the Sand Dunes terrace.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> the First Emperor died at the Sand Dunes terrace.

sentences.zh: 丞相斯為上崩在外，恐諸公子及天下有變，乃秘之不發喪，棺載轀涼車中，故幸宦者驂乘。

translations.literal: Chancellor Si, because the ruler had died abroad, feared that the various princes and all under Heaven might change; he therefore kept it secret and did not announce the mourning. The coffin was loaded into a pallbearer carriage, and favored eunuchs rode as outriders on the team.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Si, fearing unrest among the princes and the realm when the ruler died away from the capital, kept the death secret and issued no mourning announcement. The coffin was placed in a closed carriage, with favored eunuchs riding beside the driver.

sentences.zh: 所至，上食、百官奏事如故，宦者輒從車中可其奏事。

translations.literal: Wherever they arrived, meals for the ruler and memorials from the hundred officials proceeded as before; the eunuchs would at once approve their memorials from inside the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they stopped, the ruler's meals and officials' memorials continued as usual; eunuchs would approve memorials from inside the carriage.

sentences.zh: 獨胡亥、趙高及幸宦者五六人知之。

translations.literal: Only Huhai, Zhao Gao, and some five or six favored eunuchs knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huhai, Zhao Gao, and five or six favored eunuchs knew.

sentences.zh: 初，始皇尊寵蒙氏，信任之。

translations.literal: Earlier the First Emperor had honored and favored the Meng clan and trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the First Emperor had honored and trusted the Meng clan.

sentences.zh: 蒙恬任外將，蒙毅常居中參謀議，名為忠信，故雖諸將相莫敢與之爭。

translations.literal: Meng Tian held command as an outer general; Meng Yi often took part in counsel at court. Their reputation was for loyalty and trustworthiness, so even among generals and chancellors none dared contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tian commanded in the field; Meng Yi often advised at court. Renowned for loyalty, they were unmatched even among generals and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 趙高者，生而隱宮，始皇聞其強力，通於獄法，舉以為中車府令，使教胡亥決獄，胡亥幸之。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao had been castrated at birth. The First Emperor heard that he was strong and versed in penal law; he was promoted to director of the palace carriage office and set to teach Huhai how to decide legal cases. Huhai favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao had been castrated at birth. The First Emperor, hearing he was strong and expert in penal law, made him director of the palace carriage office and had him teach Huhai to judge cases. Huhai favored him.

sentences.zh: 趙高有罪，始皇使蒙毅治之；

translations.literal: Zhao Gao committed an offense; the First Emperor had Meng Yi try him;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Gao offended, the First Emperor had Meng Yi try him;

sentences.zh: 毅當高法應死。

translations.literal: Yi judged Gao guilty under the law and deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: Yi found Gao guilty and liable to death under the law.

sentences.zh: 始皇以高敏於事，赦之，復其官。

translations.literal: The First Emperor, because Gao was sharp in affairs, pardoned him and restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor, deeming Gao capable, pardoned him and restored his office.

sentences.zh: 趙高既雅得幸於胡亥，又怨蒙氏，乃說胡亥，請詐以始皇命誅扶蘇而立胡亥為太子。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao, having long been favored by Huhai and also bearing a grudge against the Meng clan, then persuaded Huhai, asking to forge the First Emperor's command to execute Fusu and establish Huhai as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao, already favored by Huhai and resentful of the Mengs, urged Huhai to forge the First Emperor's order to kill Fusu and make Huhai crown prince.

sentences.zh: 胡亥然其計。

translations.literal: Huhai approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Huhai agreed to the plan.

sentences.zh: 趙高曰：「不與丞相謀，恐事不能成。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao said, “Without plotting with the chancellor, I fear the affair cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao said, “Without the chancellor's help, I fear this cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 」乃見丞相斯曰：「上賜長子書及符璽，皆在胡亥所。

translations.literal: ” He then went to see Chancellor Si and said, “The letter and tally-seal the ruler bestowed on the eldest son are both in Huhai's keeping.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then saw Chancellor Si and said, “The letter and imperial seal for the eldest son are both with Huhai.

sentences.zh: 定太子，在君侯與高之口耳。

translations.literal: Who is made crown prince rests only on your lordship's lips and Gao's.
translations.idiomatic: Who becomes crown prince is for you and me alone to decide.

sentences.zh: 事將何如？

translations.literal: How will the matter go?
translations.idiomatic: What will you do?

sentences.zh: 」斯曰：「安得亡國之言！

translations.literal: ” Si said, “How can there be talk that would ruin the state!
translations.idiomatic: ” Si said, “How can you speak of ruining the state!

sentences.zh: 此非人臣所當議也！

translations.literal: This is not what a minister ought to discuss!
translations.idiomatic: This is no business for a minister!

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「君侯材能、謀慮、功高、無怨、長子信之，此五者皆孰與蒙恬？

translations.literal: ” Gao said, “Your lordship's talent, counsel, lofty merit, freedom from enmity, and the eldest son's trust in you—in these five respects, which does not match Meng Tian?
translations.idiomatic: ” Gao said, “In talent, counsel, merit, freedom from enemies, and the eldest son's trust—in all five, who compares with Meng Tian?

sentences.zh: 」斯曰：「不及也。

translations.literal: ” Si said, “I do not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: ” Si said, “I do not.

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「然則長子即位，必用蒙恬為丞相，君侯終不懷通侯之印歸鄉里明矣！

translations.literal: ” Gao said, “Then if the eldest son takes the throne, he is sure to make Meng Tian chancellor. That your lordship will never carry the seal of a full marquis back to your home district is clear!
translations.idiomatic: ” Gao said, “Then when the eldest son reigns, Meng Tian will surely be chancellor. You will never take a full marquis's seal home—that is plain!

sentences.zh: 胡亥慈仁篤厚，可以為嗣。

translations.literal: Huhai is kind, benevolent, and sincere and may serve as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Huhai is kind and sincere—fit to be heir.

sentences.zh: 願君審計而定之！

translations.literal: I beg you to weigh the plan and decide!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh this and decide!

sentences.zh: 」丞相斯以為然，乃相與謀，詐為受始皇詔，立胡亥為太子。

translations.literal: ” Chancellor Si thought it right; they then plotted together, forged acceptance of the First Emperor's edict, and established Huhai as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: ” Si agreed; they plotted together, forged an edict from the First Emperor, and made Huhai crown prince.

sentences.zh: 更為書賜扶蘇，數以不能闢地立功，士卒多耗，〔反〕數上書<ref>〔反〕數上書據章校補。

translations.literal: They further drafted a letter bestowed on Fusu, charging him with failure to open territory and achieve merit, heavy wastage of soldiers, 〔repeatedly〕sending up memorials<ref>〔repeatedly〕sending up memorials—supplemented per Zhang's collation.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted another letter to Fusu, accusing him of failing to expand the borders and win merit, wasting many troops, and 〔repeatedly〕submitting memorials<ref>〔repeatedly〕submitting memorials—supplemented per Zhang's collation.

translations.idiomatic: </ref> with insolent slander, day and night resenting that he was not recalled as crown prince; General Tian did not correct him, knowing his intent—all were ordered to die, and the army was given to lieutenant general Wang Li.

sentences.zh: 扶蘇發書，泣，入內舍，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Fusu received the letter, wept, went into the inner quarters, and wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fusu opened the letter, wept, went to his quarters, and prepared to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 蒙恬曰：「陛下居外，未立太子；

translations.literal: Meng Tian said, “Your Majesty is abroad and has not yet installed a crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tian said, “His Majesty is abroad and has not named a crown prince;

sentences.zh: 使臣將三十萬眾守邊，公子為監，此天下重任也。

translations.literal: your servant commands three hundred thousand men guarding the border, and the prince serves as overseer—this is a weighty charge for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I command three hundred thousand men on the frontier and you oversee us—this is a charge of the first importance.

sentences.zh: 今一使者來，即自殺，安知其非詐！

translations.literal: Now a single envoy arrives and you would at once kill yourself—how do you know it is not a fraud!
translations.idiomatic: A single envoy arrives and you would die at once—how do you know this is not a trick!

sentences.zh: 復請而後死，未暮也。

translations.literal: Ask again and then die—it is not yet evening.
translations.idiomatic: Send to verify and then die—it is not yet too late.

sentences.zh: 」使者數趣之。

translations.literal: ” The envoy repeatedly pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The envoy pressed him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 扶蘇謂蒙恬曰：「父賜子死，尚安復請！

translations.literal: Fusu said to Meng Tian, “When a father grants a son death, how can one still ask again!
translations.idiomatic: Fusu said to Meng Tian, “When a father orders his son to die, what more is there to ask!

sentences.zh: 」即自殺。

translations.literal: ” He then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” He killed himself at once.

sentences.zh: 蒙恬不肯死，使者以屬吏，繫諸陽周。

translations.literal: Meng Tian refused to die; the envoy handed him over to the clerks and had him bound at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tian refused to die; the envoy handed him to the officials and had him imprisoned at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 更置李斯舍人為護軍，還報。

translations.literal: They replaced him with a retainer of Li Si as army protector and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: They replaced him with a retainer of Li Si as army protector and returned with word.
