translations.literal: Huhai, having heard that Fusu was dead, wished at once to release Meng Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Huhai, hearing Fusu was dead, wished at once to release Meng Tian.

sentences.zh: 會蒙毅為始皇出禱山川，還至。

translations.literal: It happened that Meng Yi had gone abroad for the First Emperor to pray at mountains and rivers and was just returning.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Meng Yi returned from praying at mountains and rivers on the First Emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 趙高言於胡亥曰：「先帝欲舉賢立太子久矣，而毅諫以為不可，不若誅之！

translations.literal: Zhao Gao said to Huhai, “The late emperor long wished to raise the worthy and make him crown prince, but Yi remonstrated that it could not be done—better execute him!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao told Huhai, “The late emperor long meant to make the worthy crown prince, but Yi dissuaded him—better kill him!

sentences.zh: 」乃繫諸代。

translations.literal: ” He was then bound at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was imprisoned at Dai.

sentences.zh: 遂從井陘抵九原。

translations.literal: They then went from Jingxing to Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then traveled from Jingxing to Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 會暑，轀車臭，乃詔從官令車載一石鮑魚以亂之。

translations.literal: It being hot, the pallbearer carriage stank; they then ordered the following officials to load a picul of salted fish in their carts to mask it.
translations.idiomatic: In the heat the carriage stank; they ordered attendants to load a picul of salted fish in each cart to mask the smell.

sentences.zh: 從直道至咸陽，發喪。

translations.literal: They followed the Imperial Highway to Xianyang and announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: They took the Imperial Highway to Xianyang and announced the death.

sentences.zh: 太子胡亥襲位。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huhai succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huhai succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 九月，葬始皇於驪山，下錮三泉；

translations.literal: In the ninth month they buried the First Emperor at Mount Li, securing the Three Springs below;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they buried the First Emperor at Mount Li, sealing the Three Springs beneath;

sentences.zh: 奇器珍怪，徙藏滿之。

translations.literal: curiosities and rare wonders were moved in until it was full.
translations.idiomatic: rare objects and curiosities were moved in until it was full.

sentences.zh: 令匠作機弩，有穿近者輒射之。

translations.literal: They ordered craftsmen to make crossbow triggers so that anyone who broke in nearby was shot at once.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen made triggered crossbows to shoot anyone who broke in.

sentences.zh: 以水銀為百川、江河、大海，機相灌輸。

translations.literal: They used mercury for the hundred streams, rivers, and the great sea, with mechanisms to pour and circulate it.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury formed the hundred streams, rivers, and sea, pumped by mechanisms.

sentences.zh: 上具天文，下具地理。

translations.literal: Above were set out the patterns of heaven; below, the forms of earth.
translations.idiomatic: The ceiling bore the heavens; the floor, the earth.

sentences.zh: 後宮無子者，皆令從死。

translations.literal: Concubines of the rear palace who had borne no sons were all ordered to follow in death.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines who had borne no sons were all ordered to die with him.

sentences.zh: 葬既已下，或言工匠為機藏，皆知之，藏重即泄。

translations.literal: Once the burial was completed below, some said the craftsmen who made the hidden triggers all knew the secret; when the treasure was heavy, news would leak.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, some said the craftsmen who built the traps knew the layout; once the treasure was sealed in, the secret would leak.

sentences.zh: 大事盡，閉之墓中。

translations.literal: When the great work was finished, they shut them inside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, they sealed the craftsmen inside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 3二世欲誅蒙恬兄弟。

translations.literal: 3 The Second Emperor wished to execute the Meng brothers.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The Second Emperor wished to kill the Meng brothers.

sentences.zh: 二世兄子子嬰諫曰：「趙王遷殺李牧而用顏聚，齊王建殺其故世忠臣而用後勝，卒皆亡國。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor's elder brother's son Ziying remonstrated, saying, “King Qian of Zhao killed Li Mu and employed Yan Ju; King Jian of Qi killed his hereditary loyal ministers and employed Hou Sheng—in the end both states perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor's nephew Ziying remonstrated: “King Qian of Zhao killed Li Mu and used Yan Ju; King Jian of Qi killed his old loyal ministers and used Hou Sheng—both states fell in the end.

sentences.zh: 蒙氏，秦之大臣謀士也，而陛下欲一旦棄去之。

translations.literal: The Meng clan are great ministers and strategists of Qin, yet Your Majesty wishes to cast them off in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The Mengs are Qin's great ministers and strategists, yet Your Majesty would cast them off at once.

sentences.zh: 誅殺忠臣而立無節行之人，是內使群臣不相信，而外使鬥士之意離也。

translations.literal: To execute loyal ministers and establish men without integrity is inwardly to make the hundred officials disbelieve you and outwardly to make fighting men's hearts turn away.
translations.idiomatic: To kill loyal ministers and elevate men without principle is to lose your officials within and your warriors without.

sentences.zh: 」二世弗聽，遂殺蒙毅及內史恬。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor would not listen and then killed Meng Yi and Interior Secretary Tian.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor would not listen and killed Meng Yi and Interior Secretary Tian.

sentences.zh: 恬曰：「自吾先人及至子孫，積功信於秦三世矣。

translations.literal: Tian said, “From my forebears down to my sons and grandsons, we have heaped merit trusted in Qin for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said, “From my ancestors to my descendants, we have served Qin with trusted merit for three generations.

sentences.zh: 今臣將兵三十餘萬，身雖囚繫，其勢足以倍畔。

translations.literal: Now your servant commands more than three hundred thousand troops; though my person is bound, the force is enough to rebel twofold.
translations.idiomatic: I now command more than three hundred thousand men; though imprisoned, my power is enough to rebel twice over.

sentences.zh: 然自知必死而守義者，不敢辱先人之教，以不忘先帝也。

translations.literal: Yet one who knows he must die yet holds to righteousness dares not disgrace his ancestors' teaching, so as not to forget the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing I must die, I hold to righteousness and dare not disgrace my ancestors' teaching or forget the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 」乃吞藥自殺。

translations.literal: ” He then swallowed poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” He swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: ::揚子《法言》曰：或問：「蒙恬忠而被誅，忠奚可為也？

translations.literal: :: Yang Xiong's Fayan says: Someone asked, “Meng Tian was loyal yet was executed—how can loyalty be practiced?
translations.idiomatic: :: Yang Xiong's Fayan says: Someone asked, “Meng Tian was loyal yet was executed—what good is loyalty?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「漸山，堙谷，起臨洮，擊遼水，力不足而尸有餘，忠不足相也。

translations.literal: ” The answer was, “Gradual mountains, dammed valleys, rising from Lintao, striking to the Liao River—strength insufficient yet corpses in surplus; loyalty insufficient to set against it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The answer was, “Mountains piled, valleys filled, from Lintao to the Liao—strength fell short yet corpses piled up; loyalty is no match for that.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：秦始皇方毒天下而蒙恬為之使，恬不仁不知矣。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: The First Emperor was just then poisoning all under Heaven, and Meng Tian served as his instrument—Tian was unkind and unknowing indeed.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: The First Emperor was poisoning the realm, and Meng Tian served him—Tian was neither humane nor wise.

sentences.zh: 然恬明於為人臣之義，雖無罪見誅，能守死不貳，斯亦足稱也。

translations.literal: Yet Tian was clear on the duty of a minister; though guiltless he was executed, he could hold to death without wavering—that too is enough to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tian understood a minister's duty; though executed without guilt, he held to death without wavering—that too deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，戊寅，大赦。

translations.literal: 1 Winter, tenth month, wuyin—a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Winter, tenth month, wuyin—a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 2春，二世東行郡縣，李斯從；

translations.literal: 2 In spring the Second Emperor traveled east through the commanderies and counties; Li Si followed;
translations.idiomatic: 2 In spring the Second Emperor toured the eastern commanderies and counties; Li Si accompanied him;

sentences.zh: 到碣石，並海，南至會稽；

translations.literal: he reached Jieshi, followed the sea, and went south as far as Kuaiji;
translations.idiomatic: he reached Jieshi, followed the coast south to Kuaiji;

sentences.zh: 而盡刻始皇所立刻石，旁著大臣從者名，以章先帝成功盛德而還。

translations.literal: and had every stone the First Emperor had carved re-inscribed, with the names of accompanying ministers added beside, to display the late emperor's achievements and splendid virtue, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: had every inscription the First Emperor had carved renewed, with the names of accompanying ministers added, to proclaim the late emperor's achievements and virtue, then returned.

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month—the Second Emperor reached Xianyang and said to Zhao Gao, “A man's life in the world is like six swift steeds galloping past a crack.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month—the Second Emperor reached Xianyang and told Zhao Gao, “Life in this world is like six swift horses flashing past a crack.

sentences.zh: 吾既已臨天下矣，欲悉耳目之所好，窮心志之所樂，以終吾年壽，可乎？

translations.literal: I have already come to rule all under Heaven. I wish to satisfy everything my ears and eyes delight in and exhaust everything my heart and will enjoy, to finish out my years of life—is that possible?
translations.idiomatic: I already rule the realm. I wish to indulge every pleasure of eye and ear and exhaust every delight of heart and will to the end of my days—may I?

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「此賢主之所能行，而昏亂主之所禁也。

translations.literal: ” Gao said, “This is what a worthy ruler can do, but what a benighted and chaotic ruler forbids.

sentences.zh: 雖然，有所未可。

translations.literal: Even so, there is something not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, something stands in the way.

translations.idiomatic: Allow me to explain: over the plot at Sand Dunes, the princes and ministers all harbor doubts;

translations.literal: the various princes are all the late emperor's elder brothers, and the great ministers were moreover installed by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: the princes are all the late emperor's elder brothers, and the ministers were appointed by him.

sentences.zh: 今陛下初立，此其屬意怏怏皆不服，恐為變。

translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just ascended; they are resentful and displeased. I fear rebellion.

translations.literal: Your servant trembles in fear, dreading that the end will not come—how can Your Majesty indulge in such pleasures!
translations.idiomatic: I tremble in fear that all will not end well—how can Your Majesty seek such pleasures!

sentences.zh: 」二世曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor said, “What is to be done about it?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor said, “What should be done?

sentences.zh: 」趙高曰：「陛下嚴法而刻刑，令有罪者相坐，誅滅大臣及宗室；

translations.literal: ” Zhao Gao said, “Your Majesty should tighten the laws and sharpen punishments, make the guilty implicate one another, and execute great ministers and the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Gao said, “Tighten the laws and sharpen punishments; make the guilty implicate one another; kill the great ministers and the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 然後收舉遺民，貧者富之，賤者貴之。

translations.literal: then gather up the leftover people, enrich the poor, and ennoble the base.
translations.idiomatic: then gather up the common people, enrich the poor, and ennoble the lowly.

Then hidden merit will accrue to Your Majesty, harm will be cleared and treacherous plots stopped. translations.idiomatic: Remove all the late emperor's old ministers and appoint your own trusted men. Hidden merit will be yours, threats gone and plots blocked. Every official will bathe in your grace; you may pillow your head high and indulge as you please.

translations.idiomatic: No plan is better.

translations.idiomatic: They revised the laws to be harsher still; when ministers or princes offended, Zhao Gao was sent to try them.

translations.idiomatic: Twelve princes were executed in Xianyang market; ten princesses were crushed to death at Du; their property went to the treasury; those caught in the chain of guilt were beyond count.

translations.literal: The prince Jianglu and his three brothers by the same mother were imprisoned in the inner palace; judgment on their guilt was deferred alone.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianglu and his three full brothers were imprisoned in the inner palace; their case alone was held back.

translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor sent an envoy to Jianglu: “You are disloyal, prince—death is your due!

sentences.zh: 吏致法焉。

translations.literal: Let the clerks apply the law.
translations.idiomatic: Let the law take its course.

sentences.zh: 」將閭曰：「闕廷之禮，吾未嘗敢不從賓贊也，廊廟之位，吾未嘗敢失節也，受命應對，吾未嘗敢失辭也，何謂不臣？

translations.literal: ” Jianglu said, “At audience in the court I have never dared fail to follow the usher's prompts; in the hall of state I have never dared miss a ritual step; receiving orders and replying I have never dared miss a word—what is meant by 'not a minister'?
translations.idiomatic: ” Jianglu said, “At court I never failed the usher's cues; in the hall I never missed a step of ritual; in receiving orders I never misspoke—what disloyalty is this?

sentences.zh: 願聞罪而死！

translations.literal: I wish to hear my crime and then die!
translations.idiomatic: Let me hear my crime before I die!

translations.literal: ” The envoy said, “Your servant may not take part in counsel; I carry the letter and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: ” The envoy said, “I may not deliberate—I carry the order and obey.

sentences.zh: 」將閭乃仰天大呼「天」者三，曰：「吾無罪！

translations.literal: ” Jianglu then looked up to Heaven and thrice cried “Heaven!”, saying, “I am guiltless!
translations.idiomatic: ” Jianglu looked up and thrice cried “Heaven!”, saying, “I am guiltless!

sentences.zh: 」昆弟三人皆流涕，拔劍自殺。

translations.literal: ” The three brothers by the same mother all wept, drew their swords, and killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: ” All three brothers wept, drew their swords, and killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 宗室振恐。

translations.literal: The imperial clan trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan trembled in fear.

translations.idiomatic: I ought to have followed him in death but could not—unfilial as a son and unloyal as a minister.

translations.literal: ” Zhao Gao said, “A minister should worry about dying and have no leisure—how could he find opportunity to plot change!
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Gao said, “A minister should be too busy fearing death to plot rebellion—how could he scheme!

sentences.zh: 」二世可其書，賜錢十萬以葬。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor approved his letter and bestowed one hundred thousand cash for burial.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor approved the memorial and granted one hundred thousand cash for burial.

sentences.zh: 復作阿房宮。

translations.literal: They resumed building Epang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Work on Epang Palace was resumed.

sentences.zh: 盡徵材士五萬人為屯衛咸陽，令教射。

translations.literal: They mustered fifty thousand able-bodied men as garrison guards for Xianyang and ordered them taught archery.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand able-bodied men were conscripted to garrison Xianyang and trained in archery.

sentences.zh: 狗馬禽獸當食者多，度不足，下調郡縣，轉輸菽粟、芻稿。

translations.literal: Dogs, horses, birds, and beasts requiring feed were many; they estimated supplies would not suffice and ordered the commanderies and counties below to transport grain and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: So many dogs, horses, birds, and beasts needed feeding that supplies ran short; the court ordered the commanderies and counties to ship grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 皆令自齎糧食；

translations.literal: All were ordered to bring their own provisions;
translations.idiomatic: All were ordered to bring their own food;

sentences.zh: 咸陽三百里內不得食其穀。

translations.literal: within three hundred li of Xianyang none might eat its grain.
translations.idiomatic: and no grain within three hundred li of Xianyang might be consumed locally.

sentences.zh: 3秋，七月，陽城人陳勝、陽夏人吳廣起兵於蘄。

translations.literal: 3 Autumn, seventh month—Chen Sheng of Yangcheng and Wu Guang of Yangxia raised troops at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: 3 In autumn, the seventh month, Chen Sheng of Yangcheng and Wu Guang of Yangxia rose in arms at Qi.

sentences.zh: 是時，發閭左戍漁陽，九百人屯大澤鄉，陳勝、吳廣皆為屯長。

translations.literal: At this time men from the left lanes of the wards were being sent to garrison Yuyang—nine hundred men stationed at Daze township; Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were both platoon chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time nine hundred men from the poor lanes were being sent to garrison Yuyang and were encamped at Daze township; Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were both platoon leaders.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，道不通，度已失期。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent great rain; the roads were impassable. They estimated they had already missed the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain made the roads impassable, and they knew they would miss the deadline.

sentences.zh: 失期，法皆斬。

translations.literal: Missing the deadline—by law all were to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Missing the deadline meant death by law for all.

sentences.zh: 陳勝、吳廣因天下之愁怨，乃殺將尉，召令徒屬曰；

translations.literal: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, relying on the realm's grief and resentment, then killed the commander and adjutant, summoned the conscripts, and said:
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, seizing on popular grievance, killed the commander and adjutant, called the men together, and said:

sentences.zh: 「公等皆失期當斬，假令毋斬，而戍死者固什六七。

translations.literal: “You gentlemen have all missed the deadline and ought to be beheaded. Even if you were not beheaded, those who die on frontier service are surely six or seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: “You have all missed the deadline and face execution. Even if you were spared, six or seven in ten would die on the frontier anyway.

sentences.zh: 且壯士不死則已，死則舉大名耳！

translations.literal: Moreover, for a stalwart man, if he does not die, so be it; if he dies, let it be for a great name!
translations.idiomatic: A brave man may as well die for a great cause!

sentences.zh: 王侯將相寧有種乎！

translations.literal: Are kings, marquises, generals, and chancellors born to their stations!
translations.idiomatic: Are kings, marquises, generals, and chancellors born to their rank!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆從之。

translations.literal: ” The crowd all followed them.
translations.idiomatic: ” The men all agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，為壇而盟，稱大楚；

translations.literal: They then falsely claimed to act for Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, made an altar and swore alliance, and proclaimed Great Chu;
translations.idiomatic: They falsely claimed to act for Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, made an altar to swear alliance, and proclaimed Great Chu;

sentences.zh: 陳勝自立為將軍，吳廣為都尉。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng installed himself as general; Wu Guang as commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng made himself general and Wu Guang commandant.

sentences.zh: 攻大澤鄉，拔之。

translations.literal: They attacked Daze township and took it.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Daze township and captured it.

sentences.zh: 收而攻蘄，蘄下。

translations.literal: They gathered forces and attacked Qi; Qi fell.
translations.idiomatic: They rallied men, attacked Qi, and took it.

sentences.zh: 乃令符離人葛嬰將兵徇蘄以東，攻銍、酇、苦、柘、譙，皆下之。

translations.literal: They then ordered Ge Ying of Fuli to lead troops and march east from Qi, attacking Zhi, Zan, Ku, Zhe, and Qiao—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Ge Ying of Fuli east from Qi with troops to attack Zhi, Zan, Ku, Zhe, and Qiao—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 行收兵，比至陳，車六七百乘，騎千餘，卒數萬人。

translations.literal: As they marched they gathered troops; by the time they reached Chen there were six or seven hundred chariots, more than a thousand horsemen, and tens of thousands of foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering troops as they marched, by the time they reached Chen they had six or seven hundred chariots, more than a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry.

sentences.zh: 攻陳，陳守、尉皆不在，獨守丞與戰譙門中，不勝；

translations.literal: They attacked Chen. The commandery administrator and commandant were both away; only the assistant administrator fought them at the Qiao gate and was defeated;
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Chen. The administrator and commandant were away; only the assistant administrator fought them at the Qiao gate and was beaten;

sentences.zh: 守丞死，陳勝乃入據陳。

translations.literal: the assistant administrator died, and Chen Sheng then entered and occupied Chen.
translations.idiomatic: the assistant administrator was killed, and Chen Sheng entered and held Chen.

sentences.zh: 初，大梁人張耳、陳餘相與為刎頸交。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Er of Daliang and Chen Yu of Chenyu were sworn friends unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Er of Daliang and Chen Yu had been sworn friends unto death.

sentences.zh: 秦滅魏，聞二人魏之名士，重賞購求之。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Wei, it heard that the two were famous scholars of Wei and offered heavy rewards to hunt them down.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Wei, hearing they were renowned men of Wei, it offered heavy rewards for their capture.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘乃變名姓，俱之陳，為里監門以自食。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu then changed their names and surnames, went together to Chen, and served as ward gatekeepers to feed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu changed their names, fled together to Chen, and lived as ward gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 里吏嘗以過笞陳餘，陳餘欲起，張耳躡之，使受笞。

translations.literal: A ward officer once flogged Chen Yu for an offense. Chen Yu wished to rise; Zhang Er trod on him and made him accept the beating.
translations.idiomatic: A ward officer once flogged Chen Yu for an offense. Chen Yu started to rise; Zhang Er stepped on him and made him submit to the beating.

sentences.zh: 吏去，張耳乃引陳餘之桑下，數之曰：「始吾與公言何如？

translations.literal: When the officer had gone, Zhang Er drew Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and reproached him, saying, “At the start, what did I say to you, sir?
translations.idiomatic: When the officer left, Zhang Er took Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and rebuked him: “What did I tell you at the start?

sentences.zh: 今見小辱而欲死一吏乎！

translations.literal: Now, seeing a small humiliation, you wish to die for the sake of one petty officer!
translations.idiomatic: Will you throw your life away over a petty officer's insult!

sentences.zh: 」陳餘謝之。

translations.literal: ” Chen Yu apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Yu apologized.

sentences.zh: 陳涉既入陳，張耳、陳餘詣門上謁。

translations.literal: After Chen She had entered Chen, Zhang Er and Chen Yu went to the gate to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen She had taken Chen, Zhang Er and Chen Yu came to his gate to pay court.

sentences.zh: 陳涉素聞其賢，大喜。

translations.literal: Chen She had long heard of their worth and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She had long known their reputation and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 陳中豪傑父老請立涉為楚王，涉以問張耳、陳餘。

translations.literal: The powerful elders of Chen asked that She be made King of Chu; She put the question to Zhang Er and Chen Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's leading men asked that She be made King of Chu; She consulted Zhang Er and Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 耳、餘對曰：「秦為無道，滅人社稷，暴虐百姓。

translations.literal: Er and Yu replied, “Qin is without the Way: it has destroyed states and altars and tyrannizes the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu replied, “Qin is lawless—it has destroyed states and altars and brutalizes the people.

sentences.zh: 將軍出萬死之計，為天下除殘也。

translations.literal: The general has ventured a plan through ten thousand deaths to remove cruelty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: You have risked death to rid the realm of this tyranny.

sentences.zh: 今始至陳而王之，示天下私。

translations.literal: To reach Chen and at once declare yourself king shows the realm your private ambition.
translations.idiomatic: To declare yourself king as soon as you reach Chen will show the realm you act for yourself.

sentences.zh: 願將軍毋王，急引兵而西。

translations.literal: We wish the general not to take the royal title but urgently to lead troops west.
translations.idiomatic: Do not take the title yet; march west at once.

sentences.zh: 遣人立六國後，自為樹黨，為秦益敵。

translations.literal: Send men to install the heirs of the Six States, thereby forming factions for yourself and increasing Qin's enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Send men to restore the heirs of the Six States, build your own party, and multiply Qin's enemies.

sentences.zh: 敵多則力分，與眾則兵強。

translations.literal: When enemies are many, Qin's strength is divided; when you have the multitude, your troops are strong.
translations.idiomatic: More enemies divide Qin's strength; with allies your army grows stronger.

sentences.zh: 如此，則野無交兵，縣無守城，誅暴秦，據咸陽，以令諸侯。

translations.literal: Thus there will be no clashing armies in the open countryside and no garrisoned cities in the districts; you will execute violent Qin, hold Xianyang, and command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Then no armies will meet in the field and no counties will hold out; you can destroy Qin, seize Xianyang, and command the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 諸侯亡而得立，以德服之，〔如此〕則帝業成矣<ref>〔如此〕則帝業成矣據章校補。

translations.literal: When the feudal lords, lost and then restored, are brought to submit by virtue, 〔thus〕 the imperial enterprise will be accomplished<ref>〔Thus〕 the imperial enterprise will be accomplished—supplemented per Zhang's collation.
translations.idiomatic: When the restored lords submit to your virtue, 〔thus〕 you will achieve the imperial enterprise<ref>〔Thus〕 you will achieve the imperial enterprise—supplemented per Zhang's collation.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 今獨王陳，恐天下懈也。

translations.literal: To declare yourself king in Chen alone—I fear the realm will slacken.
translations.idiomatic: To make yourself king in Chen alone will make the realm lose heart.

sentences.zh: 」陳涉不聽，遂自立為王，號「張楚」。

translations.literal: ” Chen She would not listen and thereupon installed himself as king, with the title “Zhang Chu.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen She would not listen and declared himself king under the title Zhang Chu.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸郡縣苦秦法，爭殺長吏以應涉。

translations.literal: At this time the commanderies and counties all suffered under Qin law and vied to kill their chief officials to join Chen She.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the commanderies and counties, men groaned under Qin law and killed their officials to join Chen She.

sentences.zh: 謁者使從東方來，以反者聞。

translations.literal: An attendant envoy coming from the east reported the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant envoy arrived from the east with news of the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 二世怒，下之吏。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor was angry and handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor was furious and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 後使者至，上問之，對曰：「群盜鼠竊狗偷，郡守、尉方逐捕，今盡得，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Later envoys arrived; the ruler questioned them. They replied, “The band of thieves are rats stealing and dogs snatching; the commandery administrators and commandants are just pursuing and capturing them. Now they have all been taken—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Later envoys arrived. When questioned they said, “The rebels are mere thieves and bandits; the administrators and commandants are hunting them down and have nearly captured them all. There is no cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 」上悅。

translations.literal: ” The ruler was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 陳王以吳叔為假王，監諸將以西擊滎陽。

translations.literal: King Chen made Uncle Wu acting king to oversee the generals in attacking Xingyang from the west.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen made Wu Guang acting king to supervise the generals in the western attack on Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘復說陳王，請奇兵北略趙地。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu again urged King Chen, asking for an extraordinary force to march north and seize Zhao territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu again urged King Chen to send a special force north to overrun Zhao.

sentences.zh: 於是陳王以故所善陳人武臣為將軍，邵騷為護軍，以張耳、陳餘為左、右校尉，予卒三千人，徇趙。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Chen made Wu Chen of Chen, an old favorite, general; Shao Sao protector of the army; Zhang Er and Chen Yu left and right commandants; and gave them three thousand men to march on Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen appointed his old friend Wu Chen of Chen as general, Shao Sao as army protector, and Zhang Er and Chen Yu as left and right commandants, with three thousand men to overrun Zhao.

sentences.zh: 陳王又令汝陰人鄧宗徇九江郡。

translations.literal: King Chen also ordered Deng Zong of Ruyin to overrun Jiujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen also sent Deng Zong of Ruyin to overrun Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 當此時，楚兵數千人為聚者不可勝數。

translations.literal: At this time Chu forces gathering by the thousands could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time countless bands of Chu troops were gathering by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 葛嬰至東城，立襄彊為楚王。

translations.literal: Ge Ying reached Dongcheng and installed Xiang Qiang as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ying reached Dongcheng and made Xiang Qiang King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 聞陳王已立，因殺襄彊還報。

translations.literal: Hearing that King Chen had already been installed, he then killed Xiang Qiang and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chen She had already been crowned, he killed Xiang Qiang and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 陳王誅殺葛嬰。

translations.literal: King Chen executed Ge Ying.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen had Ge Ying executed.

sentences.zh: 陳王令〔魏人〕周市北徇魏地<ref>陳王令〔魏人〕周市北徇魏地據章校補。

translations.literal: King Chen ordered 〔the man of Wei〕 Zhou Shi to march north and overrun Wei territory<ref>King Chen ordered 〔the man of Wei〕 Zhou Shi to march north and overrun Wei territory—supplemented per Zhang's collation.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen ordered 〔the man of Wei〕 Zhou Shi north to overrun Wei<ref>King Chen ordered 〔the man of Wei〕 Zhou Shi north to overrun Wei—supplemented per Zhang's collation.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 以上蔡人房君蔡賜為上柱國。

translations.literal: He made Lord Fang Cai Ci of Shangcai grand pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: He made Cai Ci of Shangcai, Lord Fang, grand pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 陳王聞周文，陳之賢人也，習兵，乃與之將軍印，使西擊秦。

translations.literal: King Chen heard that Zhou Wen was a worthy man of Chen, skilled in warfare; he then gave him a general's seal and sent him west to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen heard that Zhou Wen of Chen was a worthy man skilled in war; he gave him a general's seal and sent him west against Qin.

sentences.zh: 武臣等從白馬渡河，至諸縣，說其豪傑，豪傑皆應之。

translations.literal: Wu Chen and the rest crossed the Yellow River at Baima, reached the various counties, and persuaded their powerful men—all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen and his force crossed at Baima, went from county to county winning over the local leaders, and all joined them.

sentences.zh: 乃行收兵，得數萬人。

translations.literal: They then marched gathering troops and obtained tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on, they gathered tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 號武臣為武信君。

translations.literal: They styled Wu Chen Lord Martial Faith.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Wu Chen the title Lord Martial Faith.

sentences.zh: 下趙十餘城。

translations.literal: They reduced more than ten cities of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than a dozen Zhao cities.

sentences.zh: 餘皆城守。

translations.literal: The rest all held their cities in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The rest held their walls.

sentences.zh: 乃引兵東北擊范陽。

translations.literal: They then led troops northeast to attack Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched northeast against Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 范陽蒯徹說武信君曰：「足下必將戰勝而後略地，攻得然後下城，臣竊以為過矣。

translations.literal: Kuai Che of Fanyang said to Lord Martial Faith, “Your lordship surely intends to win battles before seizing territory and to take cities only after storming them—your servant privately thinks this is a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Che of Fanyang told Lord Martial Faith, “You mean to win every battle before advancing and storm every city before taking it—I think that is a mistake.

sentences.zh: 誠聽臣之計，可不攻而降城，不戰而略地，傳檄而千里定，可乎？

translations.literal: If you truly heed your servant's plan, you can take cities without attacking and seize territory without fighting; send a proclamation and secure a thousand li—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: If you follow my plan, you can take cities without siege and land without battle—a proclamation could settle a thousand li. Will you hear it?

sentences.zh: 」武信君曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: ” Lord Martial Faith said, “What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: ” Lord Martial Faith asked, “What do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」徹曰：「范陽令徐公，畏死而貪，欲先天下降。

translations.literal: ” Che said, “Magistrate Xu of Fanyang fears death and is greedy; he wishes to submit first, before Heaven's troops arrive.
translations.idiomatic: ” Kuai Che said, “Magistrate Xu of Fanyang fears death and loves gain; he wants to surrender before you arrive.

sentences.zh: 君若以為秦所置吏，誅殺如前十城，則邊地之城皆為金城、湯池，不可攻也。

translations.literal: If your lordship treats him as an officer Qin installed and executes him as with the ten cities before, then the border cities will all become metal walls and boiling moats—impossible to attack.
translations.idiomatic: If you treat him as a Qin appointee and kill him as you did the last ten cities, every border town will become an impregnable fortress.

sentences.zh: 君若賚臣侯印以授范陽令，使乘朱輪華轂，驅馳燕、趙之郊，即燕、趙城可毋戰而降矣。

translations.literal: If your lordship rewards your servant with a marquis's seal to give the magistrate of Fanyang, and has him ride a red-wheeled carriage with carved hubs and gallop through the marches of Yan and Zhao, then the cities of Yan and Zhao can submit without battle.
translations.idiomatic: If you give me a marquis's seal for the magistrate of Fanyang and let him ride in state through Yan and Zhao, their cities will surrender without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」武信君曰：「善！

translations.literal: ” Lord Martial Faith said, “Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: ” Lord Martial Faith said, “Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」以車百乘、騎二百、侯印迎徐公。

translations.literal: ” He sent a hundred chariots, two hundred horsemen, and a marquis's seal to welcome Magistrate Xu.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent a hundred chariots, two hundred horsemen, and a marquis's seal to welcome Magistrate Xu.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙聞之，不戰以城下者三十餘城。

translations.literal: When Yan and Zhao heard of it, more than thirty cities submitted without battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and Zhao heard of this, more than thirty cities surrendered without fighting.

sentences.zh: 陳王既遣周章，以秦政之亂，有輕秦之意，不復設備。

translations.literal: King Chen, having already sent Zhou Zhang, because Qin's government was in disorder held Qin in contempt and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: After sending Zhou Zhang, King Chen, seeing Qin in disorder, grew contemptuous and ceased to take precautions.

sentences.zh: 博士孔鮒諫曰：「臣聞兵法：『不恃敵之不我攻，恃吾不可攻。

translations.literal: Erudite Kong Fu remonstrated, saying, “Your servant has heard in the art of war: ‘Do not rely on the enemy not attacking me; rely on my being unassailable.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Kong Fu remonstrated: “The art of war says: ‘Do not count on the enemy not attacking; count on your own defenses being impregnable.

sentences.zh: 』今王恃敵而不自恃，若跌而不振，悔之無及也。

translations.literal: ’ Now Your Majesty relies on the enemy and not on yourself—like falling and not rising; regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Yet you rely on the enemy and not on yourself. If you fall and do not rise, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 」陳王曰：「寡人之軍，先生無累焉。

translations.literal: ” King Chen said, “In my army, sir, do not trouble yourself.
translations.idiomatic: ” King Chen said, “Do not trouble yourself over my army, sir.

sentences.zh: 周文行收兵至關，車千乘，卒數十萬至戲，軍焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen marched gathering troops to the Pass— a thousand chariots, several hundred thousand men reaching Xi, where he encamped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen gathered troops as he marched to the Pass—a thousand chariots and several hundred thousand men—and camped at Xi.

sentences.zh: 二世乃大驚，與群臣謀曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: The Second Emperor was then greatly alarmed and plotted with his ministers, saying, “What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor was alarmed and asked his ministers, “What shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」少府章邯曰：「盜已至，眾強，今發近縣，不及矣。

translations.literal: ” Chamberlain for the palace treasury Zhang Han said, “The robbers have already arrived and their host is strong. To mobilize the nearby counties now is too late.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chamberlain Zhang Han said, “The rebels are here in force. Troops from nearby counties cannot arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 驪山徒多，請赦之，授兵以擊之。

translations.literal: There are many convict laborers at Mount Li. I beg to pardon them, give them arms, and strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: There are many convict laborers at Mount Li. Pardon them, arm them, and send them against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」二世乃大赦天下，使章邯免驪山徒、人奴產子，悉發以擊楚軍，大敗之。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor then proclaimed a general amnesty for all under Heaven, had Zhang Han release the Mount Li convicts and the sons of bondsmen and serfs, mustered them all to strike the Chu army, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and had Zhang Han release the Mount Li convicts and sons of bondsmen, muster them all, and attack the Chu army, which was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 周文走。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen fled.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘至邯鄲，聞周章卻，又聞諸將為陳王徇地還者多以讒毀得罪誅，乃說武信君令自王。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu reached Handan. Hearing that Zhou Zhang had retreated, and also hearing that many generals who had returned after campaigning for King Chen had been condemned and executed on slander, they urged Lord Martial Faith to declare himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu reached Handan, heard that Zhou Zhang had retreated and that many generals returning from campaigns for King Chen had been executed on false charges, and urged Lord Martial Faith to make himself king.

sentences.zh: 八月，武信君自立為趙王，以陳餘為大將軍，張耳為右丞相，邵騷為左丞相；

translations.literal: In the eighth month Lord Martial Faith installed himself as King of Zhao, making Chen Yu grand general, Zhang Er right chancellor, and Shao Sao left chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lord Martial Faith declared himself King of Zhao, appointing Chen Yu grand general, Zhang Er right chancellor, and Shao Sao left chancellor;

sentences.zh: 使人報陳王。

translations.literal: he sent men to report to King Chen.
translations.idiomatic: and sent word to King Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王大怒，欲盡族武信君等家而發兵擊趙。

translations.literal: King Chen was greatly angry and wished to exterminate the families of Lord Martial Faith and the rest and send troops to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen was furious and meant to execute Wu Chen's entire family and attack Zhao.

sentences.zh: 相國房君諫曰：「秦未亡而誅武信君等家，此生一秦也；

translations.literal: Chancellor Lord Fang remonstrated, saying, “With Qin not yet destroyed, to execute the families of Lord Martial Faith and the rest is to create another Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lord Fang remonstrated: “To kill Wu Chen's family while Qin still stands is to create another Qin;

sentences.zh: 不如因而賀之，使急引兵西擊秦。

translations.literal: better to take the occasion to congratulate him and make him urgently lead troops west to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: better to congratulate him and urge him to march west against Qin at once.

sentences.zh: 」陳王然之，從其計，徙繫武信君等家宮中，封張耳子敖為成都君，使使者賀趙，令趣發兵西入關。

translations.literal: ” King Chen thought it right, followed his plan, moved and detained the families of Lord Martial Faith and the rest in the palace, enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Ao as Lord of Chengdu, sent an envoy to congratulate Zhao, and ordered them to hurry to send troops west into the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: ” King Chen agreed, followed his advice, moved Wu Chen's family into the palace as hostages, enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Ao as Lord of Chengdu, sent envoys to congratulate Zhao, and ordered them to hurry west through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘說趙王曰：「王王趙，非楚意，特以計賀王。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu said to the King of Zhao, “Your Majesty's kingship over Zhao was not Chu's intent; they congratulated you only as a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu told the King of Zhao, “Your kingship was not Chu's wish; they congratulated you only as a stratagem.

sentences.zh: 楚已滅秦，必加兵於趙。

translations.literal: Chu has already destroyed Qin and will surely add troops against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chu has already destroyed Qin and will surely turn its armies on Zhao.

sentences.zh: 願王毋西兵，北徇燕、代，南收河內以自廣。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to send troops west; march north to subdue Yan and Dai, and south seize Henei to enlarge yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty not to march west; subdue Yan and Dai in the north and take Henei in the south to expand your power.

sentences.zh: 趙南據大河，北有燕、代，楚雖勝秦，必不敢制趙；

translations.literal: Zhao holds the great river in the south and has Yan and Dai in the north; though Chu defeats Qin, it will surely not dare control Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: With the great river to the south and Yan and Dai to the north, even if Chu defeats Qin it will not dare dominate Zhao;

sentences.zh: 不勝秦，必重趙。

translations.literal: If it does not defeat Qin, it will surely value Zhao highly.
translations.idiomatic: if it fails against Qin, it will surely court Zhao's favor.

sentences.zh: 趙乘秦、楚之敝，可以得志於天下。

translations.literal: Zhao may ride Qin and Chu's exhaustion and realize its ambition under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao can exploit Qin and Chu's exhaustion to win its place in the realm.

sentences.zh: 」趙王以為然，因不西兵，而使韓廣略燕，李良略常山，張黶略上黨。

translations.literal: ” The King of Zhao thought it right; he therefore did not send troops west, but had Han Guang subdue Yan, Li Liang subdue Changshan, and Zhang Yan subdue Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: ” The King of Zhao agreed; he sent no troops west, but had Han Guang take Yan, Li Liang take Changshan, and Zhang Yan take Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 九月，沛人劉邦起兵於沛，下相人項梁起兵於吳，狄人田儋起兵於齊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Bang of Pei raised troops at Pei; Xiang Liang of Xiapi raised troops at Wu; Tian Dan of Di raised troops in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Bang of Pei rose at Pei, Xiang Liang of Xiapi at Wu, and Tian Dan of Di in Qi.

sentences.zh: 劉邦，字季，為人隆准、龍顏，左股有七十二黑子。

translations.literal: Liu Bang, styled Ji, had a high nose bridge and dragon-like countenance; on his left thigh were seventy-two black moles.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang, styled Ji, had a prominent nose and dragon-like features, with seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 愛人喜施，意豁如也。

translations.literal: He loved people and delighted in giving; his mind was open and free.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous and open-hearted.

sentences.zh: 常有大度，不事家人生產作業。

translations.literal: He often had great breadth of spirit and did not attend to household production and work.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and would not engage in farming or trade.

sentences.zh: 初為泗上亭長，單父人呂公，好相人，見季狀貌，奇之，以女妻之。

translations.literal: At first he was pavilion chief on the Si River. Lü Gong of Shanfu, who loved physiognomy, saw Ji's appearance, marveled at it, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as pavilion chief on the Si. Lü Gong of Shanfu, a physiognomist, was struck by Ji's looks and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 既而季以亭長為縣送徒驪山，徒多道亡。

translations.literal: Later Ji, as pavilion chief, was charged by the county to escort convict laborers to Mount Li; many of the convicts fled on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as pavilion chief, Ji was sent to escort convict laborers to Mount Li; many fled along the way.

sentences.zh: 自度比至皆亡之，到豐西澤中亭，止飲，夜，乃解縱所送徒曰：「公等皆去，吾亦從此逝矣！

translations.literal: He reckoned that by the time they arrived all would have fled; reaching the pavilion in the marsh west of Feng, he halted to drink. At night he then released the convicts he was escorting, saying, “You gentlemen all go—I too will depart from here!
translations.idiomatic: Judging that none would remain by arrival, he stopped at the pavilion in the marsh west of Feng. That night he freed the convicts, saying, “Go, all of you—I am leaving too!

sentences.zh: 」徒中壯士願從者十餘人。

translations.literal: ” Among the convicts, stalwart men willing to follow numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: ” More than ten strong men among the convicts chose to follow him.

sentences.zh: 劉季被酒，夜徑澤中，有大蛇當徑，季拔劍斬蛇。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, drunk, went by night through the marsh; a great serpent blocked the path, and Ji drew his sword and cut it down.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Liu Ji cut through the marsh by night; a great serpent blocked the path, and he slew it with his sword.

sentences.zh: 有老嫗哭曰：「吾子，白帝子也，化為蛇，當道。

translations.literal: An old woman wept, saying, “My son was the White Emperor's son, transformed into a serpent, blocking the road.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman wept: “My son was the White Emperor's son, turned into a serpent blocking the road.

sentences.zh: 今赤帝子殺之！

translations.literal: Now the Red Emperor's son has killed him!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Red Emperor's son has killed him!

sentences.zh: 」因忽不見。

translations.literal: ” She then suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: ” She vanished at once.

sentences.zh: 劉季亡匿於芒、碭山澤〔巖石〕之間<ref>劉季亡匿於芒碭山澤〔巖石〕之間據章校、《史記·高祖本紀》補。

translations.literal: Liu Ji hid himself among the marshes of Mang and Dang mountains 〔rock caves〕<ref>Liu Ji hid among the marshes of Mang and Dang mountains 〔rock caves〕—supplemented per Zhang's collation and the Shiji, “Annals of Gaozu.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji hid in the marshes of Mang and Dang mountains 〔among rock caves〕<ref>Liu Ji hid in the marshes of Mang and Dang mountains 〔among rock caves〕—supplemented per Zhang's collation and the Shiji, “Annals of Gaozu.”

sentences.zh: 案：「巖石」，即岩洞也。

translations.literal: Note: “rock caves” means cave grottoes.
translations.idiomatic: Note: “rock caves” means cave grottoes.

sentences.zh: </ref>，數有奇怪；

translations.literal: </ref> strange things occurred repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: </ref> and strange portents multiplied;

sentences.zh: 沛中子弟聞之，多欲附者。

translations.literal: the young men of Pei heard of it, and many wished to join him.
translations.idiomatic: young men of Pei heard of this and many wished to follow him.

sentences.zh: 及陳涉起，沛令欲以沛應之。

translations.literal: When Chen She rose, the magistrate of Pei wished to answer with Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen She rebelled, the magistrate of Pei wished to join the uprising.

sentences.zh: 掾、主吏蕭何、曹參曰：「君為秦吏，今欲背之，率沛子弟，恐不聽。

translations.literal: The clerks and chief clerks Xiao He and Cao Shen said, “You are a Qin official; now you wish to turn against Qin and lead the young men of Pei—I fear they will not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks Xiao He and Cao Shen said, “You are a Qin official; if you turn rebel and lead the men of Pei, they may refuse to follow.

sentences.zh: 願君召諸亡在外者，可得數百人，因劫眾，眾不敢不聽。

translations.literal: We beg you to summon those who have fled and are abroad—you can get several hundred men, then coerce the multitude, and the multitude will not dare disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Summon the fugitives outside the city—you can gather hundreds—and then coerce the crowd; none will dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 」乃令樊噲召劉季。

translations.literal: ” They then had Fan Kuai summon Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: ” They sent Fan Kuai to fetch Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 劉季之眾已數十百人矣。

translations.literal: Liu Ji's following already numbered several tens and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji already had several hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 沛令後悔，恐其有變，乃閉城城守，欲誅蕭、曹。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Pei repented, fearing trouble; he closed the city and held it, wishing to execute Xiao and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate repented, fearing a coup; he shut the gates and planned to kill Xiao He and Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 蕭、曹恐，逾城保劉季。

translations.literal: Xiao and Cao were afraid; they climbed over the wall and took refuge with Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He and Cao Shen fled over the wall to Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 劉季乃書帛射城上，遺沛父老，為陳利害。

translations.literal: Liu Ji then wrote on silk, shot it onto the wall, and sent it to the elders of Pei, setting forth advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji shot a message on silk over the wall to the elders of Pei, explaining the stakes.

sentences.zh: 父老乃率子弟共殺沛令，開門迎劉季，立以為沛公。

translations.literal: The elders then led the young men together to kill the magistrate of Pei, opened the gates, and welcomed Liu Ji, establishing him as Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The elders led the young men to kill the magistrate, opened the gates, welcomed Liu Ji, and made him Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 蕭、曹等為收沛子弟，得二三千人，以應諸侯。

translations.literal: Xiao, Cao, and the rest gathered the young men of Pei and got two or three thousand men to answer the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He, Cao Shen, and others mustered two or three thousand men from Pei to join the allied lords.

sentences.zh: 項梁者，楚將項燕子也，嘗殺人，與兄子籍避仇吳中。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang was the grandson of the Chu general Xiang Yan; he had once killed a man and, with his elder brother's son Yu, fled a blood feud to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang was grandson of the Chu general Xiang Yan; after killing a man he fled with his nephew Yu to Wu to escape a feud.

sentences.zh: 吳中賢士大夫皆出其下。

translations.literal: The worthy scholar-officials of Wu all ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's leading gentlemen all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 籍少時學書，不成，去；

translations.literal: Yu in youth studied writing but did not succeed and left it;
translations.idiomatic: Yu studied writing in youth but gave it up;

sentences.zh: 學劍，又不成。

translations.literal: he studied swordsmanship, and again did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: he studied swordsmanship and failed again.

sentences.zh: 項梁怒之。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang was angry with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang was furious.

sentences.zh: 籍曰：「書，足以記名姓而已！

translations.literal: Yu said, “Writing is enough only to record one's name and surname!
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, “Writing is enough to record one's name!

sentences.zh: 劍，一人敵，不足學。

translations.literal: The sword—one man's foe—is not worth learning.
translations.idiomatic: The sword defeats one man—it is not worth learning.

sentences.zh: 學萬人敵！

translations.literal: Learn to be a match for ten thousand men!
translations.idiomatic: Learn to face ten thousand!

sentences.zh: 」於是項梁乃教籍兵法，籍大喜；

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Xiang Liang taught Yu military arts; Yu was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiang Liang then taught him warfare; Yu was delighted;

sentences.zh: 略知其意，又不肯竟學。

translations.literal: when he had grasped the meaning in part, he again would not finish learning.
translations.idiomatic: but once he grasped the gist he refused to finish.

sentences.zh: 籍長八尺餘，力能扛鼎，才器過人。

translations.literal: Yu was more than eight feet tall, strong enough to shoulder a cauldron; his talent and capacity surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Yu stood over eight feet, could lift a cauldron, and surpassed others in ability.

sentences.zh: 會稽守殷通聞陳涉起，欲發兵以應涉，使項梁及桓楚將。

translations.literal: Yin Tong, guardian of Kuaiji, heard that Chen She had risen and wished to raise troops to answer She, appointing Xiang Liang and Huan Chu as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tong, governor of Kuaiji, heard of Chen She's uprising and meant to raise troops in response, making Xiang Liang and Huan Chu his generals.

sentences.zh: 是時，桓楚亡在澤中。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Chu was a fugitive in the marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chu was then hiding in the marshes.

sentences.zh: 梁曰：「桓楚亡，人莫知其處，獨籍知之耳。

translations.literal: Liang said, “Huan Chu is a fugitive; no one knows where he is—only Yu knows.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, “Huan Chu is in hiding and no one knows where—only Yu knows.

sentences.zh: 」梁乃誡籍持劍居外，復入，與守坐，曰：「請召籍，使受命召桓楚。

translations.literal: ” Liang then instructed Yu to hold a sword and wait outside; he went in again and sat with the guardian, saying, “Please summon Yu to receive orders to summon Huan Chu.
translations.idiomatic: ” He told Yu to wait outside with a sword, went in, and said to the governor, “Please call Yu to receive orders to fetch Huan Chu.

sentences.zh: 」守曰：「諾。

translations.literal: ” The guardian said, “Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The governor agreed.

sentences.zh: 」梁召籍入。

translations.literal: ” Liang summoned Yu in.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang called Yu in.

sentences.zh: 須臾，梁眴籍曰「可行矣！

translations.literal: In a moment Liang winked at Yu and said, “You may act!
translations.idiomatic: Presently Liang winked at Yu: “Now!

sentences.zh: 」於是籍遂拔劍斬守頭。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Yu drew his sword and cut off the guardian's head.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yu drew his sword and struck off the governor's head.

sentences.zh: 項梁持守頭，佩其印綬。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang took the guardian's head and wore his seal cord.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang took the head and seized his seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 門下大驚，擾亂。

translations.literal: Those in attendance were greatly alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The staff panicked.

sentences.zh: 籍所擊殺數十百人，一府中皆懾伏，莫敢起。

translations.literal: Those Yu struck down numbered several tens and hundreds; throughout the office all cowered and submitted—none dared rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yu killed scores of men; everyone in the office cowered and none dared move.

sentences.zh: 梁乃召故所知豪吏，諭以所為起大事，遂舉吳中兵，使人收下縣，得精兵八千人。

translations.literal: Liang then summoned bold officials he had known before, explained why he was raising a great affair, and thereupon raised the troops of Wu, sending men to take the lower counties and getting eight thousand picked soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang rallied his old allies among the bold officials, explained his plan, raised Wu's armies, and seized the lower counties for eight thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 梁為會稽守，籍為裨將，徇下縣。

translations.literal: Liang became guardian of Kuaiji; Yu became lieutenant general, subduing the lower counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made himself governor of Kuaiji; Yu became lieutenant general and pacified the counties.

sentences.zh: 籍是時年二十四。

translations.literal: Yu was at this time twenty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 田儋〔者〕<ref>田儋〔者〕據章校補。

translations.literal: Tian Dan 〔was one〕<ref>Tian Dan 〔was one〕—supplemented per Zhang's collation.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan 〔was one〕<ref>Tian Dan 〔was one〕—supplemented per Zhang's collation.

sentences.zh: </ref>，故齊王族也。

translations.literal: </ref> of the former Qi royal clan.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> of the former Qi royal house.

sentences.zh: 儋從弟榮，榮弟橫，皆豪健，宗強，能得人。

translations.literal: Dan's younger cousin by the father's line was Rong; Rong's younger brother Heng—all were bold and strong; their clan was powerful and could win men.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Rong and Rong's brother Heng were all bold; their clan was strong and commanded loyalty.

sentences.zh: 周市徇地至狄，狄城守。

translations.literal: Zhou Shi was subduing territory as far as Di; Di closed its walls and held.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi advanced to Di, which shut its gates and resisted.

sentences.zh: 田儋詳為縛其奴，從少年之廷，欲謁殺奴，見狄令，因擊殺令，而召豪吏子弟曰：「諸侯皆反秦自立。

translations.literal: Tian Dan pretended to have bound his slave and, with young men, went to the court wishing to request permission to kill the slave; seeing the magistrate of Di, he struck and killed him, then summoned bold officials and their sons, saying, “The feudal lords have all turned against Qin and established themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan feigned binding his slave and went with youths to the magistrate's court to ask leave to kill him; he slew the magistrate, then rallied the local leaders, saying, “All the lords have rebelled against Qin and declared themselves.

sentences.zh: 齊，古之建國也；

translations.literal: Qi is an ancient founding state;
translations.idiomatic: Qi is an ancient kingdom;

sentences.zh: 儋，田氏，當王！

translations.literal: Dan of the Tian clan ought to be king!
translations.idiomatic: Dan of the House of Tian should be king!

sentences.zh: 」遂自立為齊王，發兵以擊周市。

translations.literal: ” He then established himself as King of Qi and raised troops to attack Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He made himself King of Qi and marched against Zhou Shi.

sentences.zh: 周市軍還去。

translations.literal: Zhou Shi's army withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 田儋率兵東略定齊地。

translations.literal: Tian Dan led troops east to subdue and settle Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan marched east to pacify Qi.

sentences.zh: 韓廣將兵北徇燕，燕地豪傑欲共立廣為燕王。

translations.literal: Han Guang led troops north to subdue Yan; the bold men of Yan wished together to establish Guang as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang marched north into Yan; Yan's leaders wished to make him king.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「廣母在趙，不可！

translations.literal: Guang said, “Guang's mother is in Zhao—it cannot be!
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, “My mother is in Zhao—I cannot!

sentences.zh: 」燕人曰：「趙方西憂秦，南憂楚，其力不能禁我。

translations.literal: ” The men of Yan said, “Zhao is now worried west over Qin and south over Chu; its strength cannot restrain us.
translations.idiomatic: ” They said, “Zhao is beset by Qin in the west and Chu in the south—it cannot stop us.

sentences.zh: 且以楚之強，不敢害趙王將相之家，趙獨安敢害將軍家乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, with Chu's strength, it would not dare harm the families of the King of Zhao's generals and chancellors—how would Zhao alone dare harm the general's family!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, even mighty Chu did not touch the Zhao king's ministers' families—would Zhao dare touch yours?

sentences.zh: 」韓廣乃自立為燕王。

translations.literal: ” Han Guang then established himself as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Han Guang declared himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 居數月，趙奉燕王母家屬歸之。

translations.literal: After several months Zhao escorted the King of Yan's mother and family back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Zhao sent back his mother and family unharmed.

sentences.zh: 趙王與張耳、陳餘北略地燕界，趙王間出，為燕軍所得，燕囚之，慾求割地；

translations.literal: The King of Zhao, with Zhang Er and Chen Yu, was subduing territory on the Yan border; the King of Zhao went out privately, was taken by Yan troops, and Yan imprisoned him, wishing to demand ceded territory;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao, with Zhang Er and Chen Yu, raided the Yan border; the king slipped out alone, was captured by Yan, imprisoned, and held for territorial concessions;

sentences.zh: 使者往請，燕輒殺之。

translations.literal: envoys went to negotiate, and Yan would at once kill them.
translations.idiomatic: every envoy sent to negotiate was killed.

sentences.zh: 有廝養卒走燕壁，見燕將曰：「君知張耳、陳餘何欲？

translations.literal: A groom ran to the Yan camp, saw the Yan general, and said, “Do you know what Zhang Er and Chen Yu want?
translations.idiomatic: A camp servant ran to the Yan lines and asked the general, “Do you know what Zhang Er and Chen Yu want?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「欲得其王耳。

translations.literal: ” He said, “They want to get back their king, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: ” He replied, “To recover their king, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」趙養卒笑曰：「君未知此兩人所欲也。

translations.literal: ” The Zhao groom laughed and said, “You do not yet know what these two men want.
translations.idiomatic: ” The servant laughed: “You do not understand them.

sentences.zh: 夫武臣、張耳、陳餘，杖馬棰下趙數十城，此亦各欲南面而王，豈欲為將相終已邪？

translations.literal: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu—with horsewhip in hand took dozens of Zhao cities; each of them also wished to face south and be king—how could they wish to end as generals and chancellors?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu took dozens of Zhao cities with a whip in hand; each wanted to rule as king—would they settle for being generals and chancellors forever?

sentences.zh: 顧其勢初定，未敢參分而王，且以少長先立武臣為王，以持趙心。

translations.literal: Only because their position was just settled they did not dare divide into thirds and be kings; for the moment, honoring seniority, they first established Wu Chen as king to hold Zhao's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Only because power was still unsettled did they not yet divide the realm; honoring age, they made Wu Chen king first to hold Zhao together.

sentences.zh: 今趙地已服，此兩人亦欲分趙而王，時未可耳。

translations.literal: Now Zhao territory has submitted; these two men also wish to divide Zhao and be kings—the time is not yet right, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhao is pacified, they mean to split it and reign—but the moment is not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 今君乃囚趙王，此兩人名為求趙王，實欲燕殺之，此兩人分趙自立。

translations.literal: Now you imprison the King of Zhao; these two men will ask for the King of Zhao in name but in fact wish Yan to kill him, so that the two can divide Zhao and establish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Imprison the king and they will plead for him in name while hoping you kill him—then they can divide Zhao between them.

sentences.zh: 夫以一趙尚易燕，況以兩賢王左提右挈而責殺王之罪？

translations.literal: If one Zhao is still enough to take Yan easily, how much more when two worthy kings link arms left and right and demand punishment for killing the king?
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao alone could crush Yan, what of two able kings joining forces to punish regicide?

sentences.zh: 滅燕易矣！

translations.literal: Destroying Yan would be easy!
translations.idiomatic: Yan would fall easily!

sentences.zh: 」燕將乃歸趙王，養卒為御而歸。

translations.literal: ” The Yan general then returned the King of Zhao; the groom served as driver on the return.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Yan general released the King of Zhao; the groom drove his carriage home.

sentences.zh: 4周市自狄還，至魏地，欲立故魏公子寧陵君咎為王。

translations.literal: 4 Zhou Shi returned from Di to Wei territory and wished to establish the former Wei prince, Lord Ningling Jiu, as king.
translations.idiomatic: 4 Zhou Shi returned from Di to Wei and wished to make the former Wei prince, Lord Ningling Jiu, king.

sentences.zh: 咎在陳，不得之魏。

translations.literal: Jiu was at Chen and could not reach Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu was at Chen and could not come to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏地已定，諸侯皆欲立周市為魏王。

translations.literal: Wei territory was already settled; the feudal lords all wished to establish Zhou Shi as King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei pacified, the lords all wished to make Zhou Shi king of Wei.

sentences.zh: 市曰：「天下昏亂，忠臣乃見。

translations.literal: Shi said, “When all under Heaven is in turmoil, the loyal minister then appears.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, “In chaos the loyal minister shows himself.

sentences.zh: 今天下共畔秦，其義必立魏王后乃可。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven together rebels against Qin; by right one must establish the King of Wei and only then is it permissible.
translations.idiomatic: All are rebelling against Qin; righteousness demands a king of Wei first.

sentences.zh: 」諸侯固請立市，市終辭不受；

translations.literal: ” The feudal lords firmly begged to establish Shi; Shi in the end declined and would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: ” The lords pressed him to take the throne; he refused;

sentences.zh: 迎魏咎於陳，五反，陳王乃遣之，立咎為魏王，市為魏相。

translations.literal: they welcomed Wei Jiu from Chen; five times they returned; the King of Chen then sent him; they established Jiu as King of Wei and Shi as Wei chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: they fetched Wei Jiu from Chen only after five embassies; Chen She sent him; Jiu became King of Wei and Shi became chancellor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 5是歲，二世廢衛君角為庶人，衛絕祀。

translations.literal: 5 That year the Second Emperor deposed Lord Jiao of Wey to commoner status; Wey's sacrifices ceased.
translations.idiomatic: 5 That year the Second Emperor reduced Lord Jiao of Wey to commoner rank; the house of Wey ended.
